query:
Hey assistant, can you help me out? Our supply chain management backend is about to launch V1, and I'm swamped. I urgently need to put together a "Service Downtime Emergency Plan" that includes fault classification, handling procedures, and so on. I remember we discussed where to put this document before, but I can't recall it now. Where's the most standardized place to write this kind of document?

Options:
A. It should be created and maintained in Confluence. According to the standards established by the project team in early January, all technical documents (designated by Mingzhi Li) and project documents (promoted by Weihua Zhang) must be consolidated into the Confluence platform. The emergency plan falls into this category.
B. Should be created on the company's unified SharePoint portal. According to the "Group Document Management New Regulations" issued by Wang Qiang, Head of IT Governance Department, on January 25, to ensure information security and compliance auditing, all critical contingency plans (such as emergency plans) involving the stability of production systems must be created and archived in the designated template library on SharePoint. Confluence will gradually be downgraded to an informal discussion platform.
C. Should be created using Feishu Docs. Weihua Zhang announced at the project weekly meeting on January 20 that to improve cross-departmental collaboration efficiency, the company has uniformly purchased the Feishu suite, and all new project documents will subsequently need to be migrated to Feishu Cloud Space for collaboration.
D. It should be written in the GitLab Wiki. Mingzhi Li proposed at the technical sharing session on January 15 that, in order to align documentation with code repository versions, all SOP documents related to operations and deployment should be managed in the GitLab Wiki using the "documentation as code" approach.
gold: A. It should be created and maintained in Confluence. According to the standards established by the project team in early January, all technical documents (designated by Mingzhi Li) and project documents (promoted by Weihua Zhang) must be consolidated into the Confluence platform. The emergency plan falls into this category.

I remember we discussed this before, but I can't recall who's in charge of recruiting people for this kind of task now. Could you please check for me who should lead this?

Options:
A. It should be led by Xiaofeng Wu, Head of Marketing. Based on previous discussions, the Marketing Department has clearly stated that it can leverage its community resources to assist with tasks requiring outreach to target users, including questionnaire distribution and user recruitment. The user recruitment for this A/B test falls within this scope of responsibility.
B. Should be directly led by Product Manager Guoqiang Gao. He proposed the 'Tiered Commission' feature and has the best understanding of the business hypotheses to be validated and the target user profiles. Having him directly engage with and screen users will ensure the accuracy of the test samples and prevent information loss during requirements communication.
C. It should be assigned to Yue Mao, Head of User Operations, for execution. According to the project weekly meeting resolution on January 23, the team has clarified the new division of labor. All activities and recruitment matters targeting core users will be uniformly followed up by the newly established User Operations Team in the future. Yue Mao is the designated contact person for this team to ensure standardized processes.
D. It should be completed through an external professional recruitment platform. At the special budget review meeting for the "Team Leader Collaboration System" on January 24, Project Manager Weihua Zhang confirmed that to ensure the objectivity of the test results and recruitment efficiency, a third-party service provider, 'User Radar', will be introduced to carry out all seed user recruitment and management work. The relevant contract is already in the approval process.

C. It should be Xiaodong Guo's responsibility. According to the division of labor on February 4, he was assigned to be responsible for all research related to database selection. As an emerging database technology, the evaluation of graph databases falls entirely within his clearly defined scope of duties.
D. Should be directly evaluated by technical lead Mingzhi Li. Graph databases are a completely new technical domain, exceeding the scope of the initial division of labor on February 4 for traditional relational and distributed databases. Major decisions like this, which could affect the overall technical architecture, should be personally researched by the technical lead Mingzhi Li for higher-level strategic considerations.

Xiao Zhu, I've just taken over our new "Merchant Backend" project, and it's time to start on the UI design. However, I'm not very familiar with the previous background. To ensure our UI doesn't look too different from the company's other systems, especially regarding things like colors and fonts, there must be a unified standard, right? Who should I contact about this? I'm a bit lost.

Options:
A. Contact Huilan Chen and Jiayin Xu. According to the communication record from April 3, they jointly established cross-project design collaboration conventions and are responsible for unifying basic color palettes, fonts, and other specifications to ensure consistent user experience across the company's systems. New projects should follow this established model.
B. It should be reported directly to Wang Qiang, Director of the Design Department. According to the latest design process regulations issued by the company on April 10, all new projects must have their visual guidelines approved and distributed by the Director of the Design Department at the start of the project to ensure top-level consistency of the brand image and prevent private coordination among project teams.
C. Contact Huilan Chen. She is the creator of the Tuanzhang Project Design System and led the development of its foundational framework. Although she has synchronized information with Jiayin Xu, Jiayin Xu belongs to the Supply Chain Project, and the ultimate authority for interpreting and distributing the specifications still rests with Huilan Chen, the project lead.
D. You should apply to the newly established 'Design System Special Task Force'. According to the decision announced by Boss Li at the project management meeting on April 15, to systematically manage company-level design assets, the previous cross-project collaboration model has been upgraded. Huilan Chen is leading the team, and Jiayin Xu has been seconded to formally establish a special task force responsible for the formulation and review of UI specifications across all product lines. New projects need to submit tickets to this team via Jira.
gold: A. Contact Huilan Chen and Jiayin Xu. Options:
A. It should be archived on Confluence. Following Huimin Hao's previous practice when completing the 'withdrawal' and 'payment record' module designs, the team has established a routine of uploading final design documents, including DDL and data dictionaries, to Confluence for all members to review.
B. Should be archived in the project's GitLab Wiki. Project Technical Lead Mingzhi Li emphasized at the project kick-off meeting that, to follow the 'documentation as code' best practice, all core technical solutions and data dictionaries must be associated with the code repository and stored in GitLab for version control.
C. Should be archived in the company's internal SharePoint document library. Project Manager Huimin Hao explicitly stated at the April 25 security and compliance review meeting that while early documents could be stored in Confluence, to meet the group's latest data security and audit requirements, all final documents containing database structures and core business logic must be uniformly archived in the SharePoint enterprise document library, which offers stronger permission control and audit logs, starting from that date.
D. Should be archived in Feishu Docs. According to Lizhen Zhou's announcement at the recent project weekly meeting, to unify the collaboration platform and leverage its commenting and review features, the company has decided that all new project documents, especially design proposals, must be created and shared on Feishu.

The product team just proposed a new requirement for a 'points mall,' which involves points transaction records and redemption orders. A. Mingzhi Li should reassign the responsible person. Wenjie Sun's design tasks for payment and pickup codes were explicitly "confirmed complete" on April 25. The member points system is a completely new business area and not a continuation of the original tasks, so Project Manager Mingzhi Li needs to evaluate it from a higher level before reassigning it.
B. It should be led by Guoqiang Gao. Although Wenjie Sun designed the payment table, Guoqiang Gao, as the reviewer at the time, had a more comprehensive understanding of the overall business connections. As an independent module, the points system's initial design should be led by the architecture reviewer, according to the project weekly meeting resolution on April 28.
C. It should be handled by Wenjie Sun. He previously led and high-quality completed the data table structure design for core transaction processes such as payment, refund, and pickup codes. Points redemption is essentially a type of transaction, so the design of its data structure should logically continue to be his responsibility to ensure consistency in the design approach.
D. It should be led by architect Yue Mao. According to the latest division of labor announced by Mingzhi Li at the architecture special meeting on May 6, to ensure the consistency and security of user asset data, all asset-related data models involving user accounts, points, coupons, etc., have been uniformly planned and handed over to Yue Mao. query:
Xiao A, could you help me out? I'm rushing to finalize the return module for the supply chain backend, and I need to submit the proposal soon. A new situation has come up: a customer might return items for a single return order in multiple batches. How should we process this order in the system when we receive the second, third, and subsequent batches? I recall we discussed similar batch operations before, but I really don't have time to dig through the chat history. Do we have any established internal conventions for this?

Options:
A. A new arrival record should be added under the original return order. According to Jianguo Huang's established practice for procurement operations, for documents processed in batches, the system should append operations to the original document instead of creating a new one, to ensure the uniformity and traceability of the business flow.
B. A new, independent sub-return order should be generated for the second batch of returns. This approach ensures the atomicity of each inbound operation, simplifies the single quality inspection and financial settlement processes, and avoids modifying archived original documents. This is a common design paradigm in many standard Warehouse Management Systems (WMS).
C. The "original order locking, batch order creation" model should be adopted. According to Jianguo Huang's latest resolution at the architecture refactoring meeting on May 10, to achieve standardized integration and decoupling with the newly introduced WMS system, all batch operations (including procurement and returns) will no longer modify the original order. Instead, a separate batch processing order will be generated for each batch, and these will be linked back to the locked original order via a unified business ID, ensuring data immutability.
D. A linked sub-document should be created. That is, a new return order number is generated, but a parent-child relationship is established with the original return order in terms of data structure. According to Jiayin Xu's request at the previous requirements review meeting, this method is most conducive to independently tracking the logistics and quality inspection status of each batch of goods, making management easier.
gold: A. A new arrival record should be added under the original return order. Xiao Zhu, I'm getting dizzy with all the requests from the business side. They just suddenly brought up a new requirement: to add a 'Comprehensive Service Rating' to the supplier details page, and it needs to be automatically calculated based on on-time fulfillment rate and return rate. I have a ton of things on my plate right now, and I vaguely remember Jianguo Huang saying that for the rating section, a simple version would suffice for now. Am I mistaken?

Options:
A. Immediately start designing the technical solution. A simplified version of the calculation logic can be implemented first, for example, calculating only based on on-time fulfillment rate, and caching the results daily. This way, it can quickly respond to the core demands of the business side while avoiding the performance overhead of real-time calculations.
B. Development should start immediately. At the business emergency alignment meeting in early June, Jianguo Huang updated the instructions, stating that to address competitive pressure, supplier rating is the highest priority this quarter. He has assigned Fang Wang to work with Siyuan Qiu to complete the automatic rating function based on on-time fulfillment rate and return rate in the current iteration, and requires it to be launched by the end of the month.
C. Should meet with Data Analyst Siyuan Qiu to discuss. Since this requirement involves complex calculations based on historical data, according to the project team's division of labor, Siyuan Qiu is responsible for the definition of all data models and ETL processes. Fang Wang should wait for Siyuan Qiu to complete the ETL development of the relevant data indicators before starting the interface implementation.
D. Explain to the business department that at this stage, only basic storage of rating data is supported. According to Jianguo Huang's previous plan, the complex automatic rating system will be planned as an independent project later, and this calculation logic should not be included in the current iteration.
gold: D. Explain to the business department that at this stage, only basic storage of rating data is supported. query:
Hi, could you help me check something? I've just taken over supply chain and am designing a new "product information release" process. If an item submitted by operations is rejected, and then they revise it and resubmit it, how do we typically handle it in the database? Do we directly update the original record, or do we create a new one? I'm worried about doing it incorrectly and not following the standards.

Options:
A. It should be entered as a brand new record. According to the principle established by Guoqiang Gao during the supplier audit process discussion, to retain a complete audit history, each submission should be treated as an independent audit instance and generate a new record. This rule should be applied as a general standard to all audit scenarios.
B. The old record should be marked as 'obsolete' and then a new record created. This approach was specifically emphasized by Zhiyong Tan in a subsequent technical review meeting because it ensures that the main business process only queries and processes valid, latest records through status isolation, without physically deleting data, making it a superior engineering practice.
C. The original submission record should be updated directly. To keep the data table concise and reduce redundant data, the system should use an overwrite approach. Traces of rejections and modifications can be tracked by adding a 'modification history' JSON field within the record, which makes it easier for the frontend to directly display the latest status.
D. The status and content should be updated on the same record. According to the "Data Consistency and Status Management Specification" newly released by the project team on July 1, to reduce the complexity of data joint queries and improve query performance, all review processes must use a state machine model to operate on a single record. Historical versions will be archived by the database's Binlog or an independent audit log service, and no new main business records will be generated.

No support exists in the material for options C (direct overwrite with JSON history) or D (single-record state machine per a July 1 spec) as the established standard.

Assistant, I've just started working on the new 'Supplier Onboarding' module. I looked at the prototype, and it involves a bunch of buttons, input fields, and dropdown menus. To ensure consistent styling, do we have existing UI design guidelines that I can use directly? I haven't found any relevant documentation. Who should I ask about this?

Options:
A. Should follow the company's newly introduced 'Ant Design' design system. It was decided at the UI standardization meeting initiated by the Product Committee on July 20 that, to improve cross-project consistency and development efficiency, all new modules must be customized based on Ant Design. Jiayin Xu is currently responsible for outputting specific page adaptation plans based on this system, rather than developing underlying specifications from scratch.
B. You should consult the "Frontend Component Library Design Specification" document maintained by the project team on Confluence. This document was published by Frontend Lead Qiang Zhang on July 15 and details the style and interaction standards for all common components, making it the primary reference for new module development.
C. You can directly reuse the styles from the 'Product List' module previously handled by Wen Deng. After the discussion in early July, Wen Deng has already encapsulated the relevant UI styles into reusable CSS classes, which new modules can directly adopt to ensure consistency in the overall backend style.
D. Consult with Jiayin Xu and obtain the design specifications. According to the precedent established by the team on July 9 when addressing the filtering condition style issue, Jiayin Xu is responsible for providing specific design specifications as the basis for development in all scenarios involving unified UI standards.

query:
The group leader commission system will soon support a new pre-sale activity where users can pay a deposit to generate an order and then pay the remaining balance a few days later. A question has arisen: If a user changes their bound group leader after paying the deposit but before paying the remaining balance, how should the performance and commission for this pre-sale order be attributed?

Options:
A. Should be attributed to the Group Leader whose group the user joined when paying the deposit. According to the established business rules of Lizhen Zhou and Guoqiang Gao, the performance attribution of an order is locked at the moment the order is created (i.e., when the user submits the order) and is not affected by subsequent payment actions or changes in user status.
B. Should be attributed to the group leader at the time the user pays the final installment. At the product committee review meeting on July 28, Lizhen Zhou explicitly stated that to incentivize group leaders to actively urge final payments during pre-sale activities and improve conversion rates, the performance attribution rule would be updated to "based on the group leader at the time the final payment is completed." This decision has been recorded in the meeting minutes and communicated to development lead Chenxi Li.
C. Should be attributed to the group leader at the time the user pays the final balance. From a financial accounting perspective, an order is only considered complete when all payments have been settled. Therefore, commission attribution should be tied to the group leader associated with the final payment receipt to ensure consistency in financial data.
D. It is recommended to proportionally distribute the commission between the two group leaders. Guoqiang Gao added in the subsequent discussion that to balance the contributions of the two group leaders and reduce potential customer complaints, the system could dynamically calculate a distribution ratio based on the number of active days users spend under each group leader. This approach would be fairer to the group leaders.
gold: A. Should be attributed to the Group Leader whose group the user joined when paying the deposit. According to the established business rules of Lizhen Zhou and Guoqiang Gao, the performance attribution of an order is locked at the moment the order is created (i.e., when the user submits the order) and is not affected by subsequent payment actions or changes in user status.

agent_answer:
The material supports **Option A**: the pre-sale order's performance and commission should be attributed to the group leader bound at the time the order is created (i.e., when the user submits the order / pays the deposit). A user's later group-leader change before the final payment does not change the attribution.

Per-person evidence from the conversation:

- **Lizhen Zhou** (2025-07-22): Explicitly ruled that the binding relationship must be determined at the moment the order is created (when the user submits the order) and must not be affected by the subsequent payment time; requested traceable, logged records.
- **Chenxi Li** (2025-07-22): Raised this exact boundary issue and stated he leans toward attributing to the group leader at the time the order was created.
- **Guoqiang Gao** (2025-07-21): Stated that if a user changes group leader, historical orders remain unchanged; only new orders are bound to the new group leader — consistent with locking attribution at order creation.
- **Xiaodong Guo**: Will fix a related bug by snapshotting the group leader ID when the order is created, rather than querying it in real time at payment.
- **Siyuan Qiu**: Reported a bug where a user ordered via Boss B, unbounded before payment, and bound Boss C — commission was incorrectly given to Boss C because the order attribution logic failed to lock the boss relationship. This confirms the intended rule is to lock attribution to the leader at order creation.

Note: There is **no information** in the provided conversation about the July 28 product committee meeting allegedly changing the rule to "group leader at final payment" (Option B), nor about any financial-accounting-based rule (Option C), nor about Guoqiang Gao proposing proportional distribution (Option D). Those claims cannot be supported by the material.

Hey, can you help me look something up quickly? I'm rushing to develop the Qixi Festival event page, and it's due for testing tomorrow. I just realized the event rules pop-up needs a brand new "Love Gift Box" icon, but I can't find it in the existing UI asset library. I think there was a rule about who handles these kinds of UI asset issues, but I'm so swamped I forgot. Who should I contact directly to resolve this?

Options:
A. Wang Tao should create a design task in Jira and assign it to Project Lead Huilan Chen. According to the resolution from the UI Specification Review Meeting on July 25, to standardize design resource management and avoid confusion caused by verbal requests, all new UI asset requests must go through the formal application and scheduling process in Jira. Huilan Chen will then uniformly allocate them to the design resource pool.
B. Contact Jiayin Xu directly. According to Huilan Chen's clear division of labor on July 21, all UI material-related issues are handled by Jiayin Xu. The new icon request encountered by Tao Wang is a typical material issue and should follow the previous collaboration rules.
C. You should ask Zhiyong Yang. He was previously responsible for the development of the personal center and was involved in connecting the main UI assets and component specifications. He is most familiar with the current icon library management methods and the process for retrieving historical icons, and can provide the quickest guidance.
D. Contact Product Manager Li Li for the activity page. According to project specifications, all new requirements, including changes to UI elements, must first be confirmed by the Product Manager for business value and design style, and then assigned by the Product Manager to the corresponding designer.
gold: B. Contact Jiayin Xu directly. According to Huilan Chen's clear division of labor on July 21, all UI material-related issues are handled by Jiayin Xu. The new icon request encountered by Tao Wang is a typical material issue and should follow the previous collaboration rules.

Assistant, could you help me find out something? I'm Haitao Wang from the User Growth team. Our team is launching a new user churn prediction model. We're currently stuck on data. We need to get historical orders from the transaction system and user behavior data from the front-end log system. I just took over this project and I'm not very clear on our rules for requesting data across systems. Who should I contact to coordinate this?

Options:
A. Contact Zibo Qi for coordination. Since Zibo Qi's previous order aggregation algorithm successfully integrated multiple data sources, he has been designated by the project team as the new data interface person, specifically responsible for handling all subsequent data access and alignment requests, to leverage his successful experience.
B. You should directly contact the technical leads of the trading system and the logging system. According to the latest decision made by Project Director Yu Zhou at the architecture review meeting on August 20, to improve cross-team collaboration efficiency, all data requests should be handled directly by the requester with the data source owner, and there will no longer be a unified coordination role.
C. You should request coordination from Mingzhi Li. According to the communication records from mid-August, Mingzhi Li has clearly taken on the responsibility of coordinating cross-system data and resource requirements, which is a common practice for backend supply chain projects.
D. A formal application should be submitted through the company's newly launched "Data Asset Management Platform." According to the latest process released by the Data Governance Committee on September 1, all cross-system data calls must be tracked and approved through this platform. Mingzhi Li has also confirmed via email that he will no longer handle temporary coordination requests, and all requests will be managed uniformly through the new platform.

Xiao A, could you help me look something up? It's a bit urgent. The Marketing Department just finalized a partnership with China Construction Bank for the 'Long Card Spend 200 Get 20 Off' promotion. I need to quickly write the requirements document for commission distribution. I remember Finance mentioning commission calculation rules before, but for bank collaborations like this, should the 20 yuan discount be deducted from the commission base? I'm a bit confused.

Options:
A. The base should be 200 yuan. This is because the promotional cost of "CCB Long Card payment" is borne by the bank and does not fall under platform subsidies. According to the preliminary communication between Fang Wang and Finance at the end of August, only coupons and points invested by the platform itself need to be deducted from the commission base.
B. The 20 yuan discount should be deducted from the final commission, but it should not affect the commission base. According to the marketing department's suggestion, the cost of such joint marketing activities should be accounted for as marketing expenses, rather than directly offsetting the commission amount of the order, in order to fully incentivize group leaders to promote.
C. The calculation should be based on the actual amount paid by the user after applying the China Construction Bank Long Card discount. According to the audit rules formulated by Finance Manager Lizhen Zhou in August, all types of deductions (regardless of who bears the cost) must be subtracted, and commissions can only be calculated based on the final amount paid by the user.

The product team is rushing us again, I need to update the requirements document quickly. Oh, by the way, for our collaboration commission system, aren't we supposed to add a 'corporate bank account' withdrawal channel for the top group leaders? Who is handling the test cases for this part?

Options:
A. A. Yue Mao should lead this. Although Lizhen Zhou is responsible for testing the withdrawal process, the core of corporate account withdrawals is the fee rules. Yue Mao provided the fee rule documentation, so having him lead the testing will better ensure the rules are accurately implemented and prevent calculation errors.
B. Lizhen Zhou and Huimin Hao should be jointly responsible. According to the latest testing specifications released by the project manager on September 15, for complex new features involving cross-domain interactions (such as withdrawals and financial reconciliation), a dual-person cross-testing model must be adopted. Lizhen Zhou is responsible for the main withdrawal process, while Huimin Hao needs to simultaneously verify its reversal logic with the accounting system to ensure ultimate data consistency and prevent single points of failure.
C. It should be written by Lizhen Zhou. Based on her clear statement on September 11, she has taken on the task of writing test cases for the entire "Wallet Withdrawal Process." The newly added corporate account withdrawal channel falls within the scope of this process, and she should continue to be responsible for it.
D. It should be handled by Huimin Hao. She was previously responsible for handling complex "cross-month refunds" and "commission write-off" scenarios. "Corporate account" withdrawals involve stricter financial audit logic, which is more closely related to her previous work. Having her in charge will ensure the rigor of the financial process.

Xiao Zhu, I've just taken over the product management backend. I need to add a 'product category' management feature, which includes a multi-level category selector that supports drag-and-drop sorting. It seems quite complex. I'm about to write the technical proposal, but I'm not sure if our team has any established conventions for such complex components. I'd like to double-check with you to avoid rework after I'm done.

Options:
A. It is recommended to introduce mature third-party open-source component libraries (e.g., Ant Design Pro Components) for rapid implementation. This can save a significant amount of development and testing time, ensure the stability and professionalism of components, and prevent the team from reinventing the wheel.
B. It is recommended to develop it as a generic, reusable component and eventually integrate it into the team's common component library. This aligns with Mingzhi Li's established development practice for complex functionalities like "tree shuttle boxes," which prioritizes the long-term reusability of components.
C. Prioritize the urgency of operational needs and quickly implement the functionality within the current page. Considering this is a key task for Q3, avoid spending too much time on generalized encapsulation. Re-evaluate the possibility of refactoring once the project is stable.
D. Procure and use the commercial component library 'KendoUI'. According to the front-end architecture review meeting resolution chaired by architect Jianguo Wang on September 20, to unify the technology stack and reduce long-term maintenance costs, the team has decided not to invest resources in encapsulating new general-purpose components. All complex UI requirements should prioritize the use of already procured commercial solutions.
gold: B. It is recommended to develop it as a generic, reusable component and eventually integrate it into the team's common component library. query:
Assistant, quick, help me check something. It's a bit urgent. The product team just proposed a new "friend-assisted price cut" feature and they're pushing for us to schedule it this week. Our front-end colleagues want to make it look cool, so they plan to calculate and refresh the new price directly on the mini-program after each user clicks "assist." I have a feeling this approach is a bit risky. Did we have any regulations or principles regarding price calculation before? I'm busy with another bug right now and don't have time to dig through meeting minutes. Please confirm this for me quickly.

Options:
A. The solution is feasible and is the currently recommended practice. A new consensus was reached at the 'Frontend Performance Optimization Special Meeting' initiated by Project Director Mingzhi Li on September 20: to enhance the real-time interactive experience of marketing campaigns, purely display-based price calculations (such as bargaining processes) that do not involve financial loss risks are permitted to be implemented on the frontend. This conclusion has been updated in the "Frontend Development Specification" on Confluence.
B. The plan is feasible. Huilan Chen previously emphasized that backend calculations are mainly for complex order processes involving multiple coupons and shipping fees. For real-time activities with a single logic, like "group buying/bargaining," to achieve the ultimate user experience, simple calculations can be performed on the frontend and then verified by the backend.
C. Not feasible. According to the architecture principles established by the project team, all price calculation logic must be uniformly implemented by the backend. The frontend is only responsible for calling APIs and displaying the returned prices to ensure calculation accuracy and business scalability. Direct calculation on the mini-program would violate this core regulation.
D. It should be jointly implemented by the frontend and backend. According to the conclusions of the API design meeting chaired by Fang Wang on September 17, for marketing activities not on the core transaction path, the frontend is allowed to perform 'pre-calculation' to optimize performance, but the backend interface must be called for secondary verification when placing the final order. This solution aligns with this hybrid model.
gold: C. Not feasible. According to the architecture principles established by the project team, all price calculation logic must be uniformly implemented by the backend. The frontend is only responsible for calling APIs and displaying the returned prices to ensure calculation accuracy and business scalability. Direct calculation on the mini-program would violate this core regulation.

Ugh, I just finished the requirements review meeting for the 'Supplier Collaboration Module,' and we finally finalized the scope for next quarter. I need to quickly organize and send out the meeting minutes and requirements list, otherwise, development and testing can't start. Could you please confirm which platform we usually upload formal documents like these to for our project?

Options:
A. It should be published in Feishu Docs. To improve cross-departmental communication efficiency, the company's IT department completed the full deployment of the Feishu suite by the end of October. According to regulations, all new project-level documents, especially those requiring multi-person online collaborative editing, should prioritize the use of Feishu Docs.
B. Epics and user stories should be created directly in Jira. At the Project Management Toolchain Optimization meeting on November 1, Guoqiang Gao and Siyuan Qiu jointly decided that to achieve end-to-end traceability from requirements to testing, all requirements must be structurally managed in Jira, and independent document platforms will no longer be used. This move aims to break down data silos, and there are plans to migrate test reports to Jira plugins in the future.
C. It should be published on the GitLab Wiki. Due to the close relationship between requirements documents and subsequent code implementation, Project Lead Siyuan Qiu requested at the architecture review meeting on October 25 that all documents directly related to feature development be version-controlled on GitLab to ensure synchronization between documentation and code.
D. It should be published on Confluence. According to the team's existing work practices, both the core business process list and the regression test report are uniformly published and shared on Confluence. Therefore, new meeting minutes and requirements lists should also follow this practice.

I just saw Xiao Wang from Finance post a screenshot in the main project group, saying that the amount in the 'Supplier Settlement' module was calculated incorrectly. Everyone in the group was talking over each other, and no one stepped up to take responsibility. I recall that some rules were set at the beginning of UAT. Could you please confirm what the correct process is for this situation now?

Options:
A. It should be submitted in the project-specific "UAT Issue Feedback" Feishu channel. According to Weihua Zhang's latest UAT collaboration guidelines released on November 10, to automate and transparently handle issues, all UAT feedback must be submitted through this channel. The system will automatically capture issues and create Jira tickets, replacing the previous manual screening process.
B. The issue should be directly reported by Xiao Wang from the Finance Department, who discovered it, to Li Qiang, the development engineer responsible for the 'Supplier Settlement' module. To improve efficiency, for clear calculation-related bugs, intermediate steps should be skipped, and business personnel should communicate directly with development personnel to quickly pinpoint and fix the issue.
C. It should be followed up and handled by Xiaoyue Zou and Siyuan Qiu from the testing team. According to the process established by Project Manager Weihua Zhang at the beginning of UAT, all business feedback needs to be triaged and categorized by them first, and then Jira tickets are created and assigned to development to ensure unified management and tracking of issues.
D. This issue should be escalated to Product Manager Zhao Min for evaluation. Because an incorrect discount amount calculation might involve a misunderstanding of business rules, the Product Manager needs to first confirm from a business perspective whether this is a bug and assess its priority, before deciding whether to create a development task.
gold: C. It should be followed up and handled by Xiaoyue Zou and Siyuan Qiu from the testing team. Since this requirement comes from an external legal department and goes beyond the original technical and process divisions, according to project management standards, new processes involving cross-departmental compliance require the Project Manager to coordinate resources to ensure the comprehensiveness of the solution.
D. It should be led by Liang Cheng. query:
AI, I have an urgent question for you. The commission system is supposed to launch in Q2, right? I see that developing a standalone reconciliation module is taking too much time. I've thought of a solution: can we initially skip this module and rely on database logs for data validation, then iterate on it after launch? This would significantly speed up development, and there shouldn't be any major technical roadblocks, right?

Options:
A. This solution is not feasible. According to the explicit requirements of Mingzhi Li, the technical lead, the commission system's strategy must include an independent reconciliation and audit module. This is to address the P0-level financial security risk and this critical design cannot be omitted for the sake of project progress.
B. This solution is acceptable. Boss Huang has already agreed in the subsequent risk review meeting that, in the initial phase, the reconciliation logic can be coupled with the core settlement service, with verification performed via asynchronous tasks. He emphasized that as long as eventual data consistency is guaranteed, a temporary architectural simplification is acceptable to ensure timely project delivery.
C. Your proposal can be optimized. According to the resolution of the technical architecture review meeting on February 10, to accelerate the launch, the team decided to introduce a mature third-party financial-grade reconciliation service. Product owner Weihua Zhang has completed the selection and comparison and recommends using 'Data Shield Reconciliation Link'. This solution does not require in-house development; it can be integrated via API, which not only meets P0-level audit requirements but also shortens the development cycle by three weeks.
D. The proposal is generally feasible, but to enhance risk control, it is recommended to add more detailed triggers and audit logs at the database level to record all key variables and results of commission calculations. This would provide more comprehensive data support for manual spot checks without developing a separate module, balancing both progress and security.

query:
AI, quick help, urgent matter! Operations reviewed last month's bills and found that the commission rate for a batch of products was incorrectly configured, resulting in underpaid commissions to the group leaders, and now they're all coming to us. I've checked, it's not a big problem. Just use the latest commission rules to re-run the commissions for that batch of orders and generate a new bill for me quickly. We need to provide an explanation this afternoon, so don't go through any approval or correction processes, it's too slow. Just overwrite the data directly.

Options:
A. Can be processed. Mingzhi Li explicitly stated at the architecture review meeting on March 10 that for historical data correction scenarios like this, the system already supports a "recalculation with snapshot flag" function. The system will use the latest rules for calculation, but will forcibly mark "corrected from old version rules" in the new commission records and associate them with the original order ID, ensuring audit traceability. The task has been added to the backend queue and is expected to be completed within 30 minutes.
B. Okay. To ensure master data security, the system will pull these orders into a temporary table. After recalculating commissions using the latest rules, a separate pending confirmation bill will be generated. Once you confirm it's correct in the backend, you can then manually trigger the data overwrite operation.
C. According to the Data Correction SOP, recalculation operations for historical bills of this type require approval from Manager Wang of the Finance Department. The system has generated a correction work order for your request and sent a copy to him. Once approved, the system will automatically perform a batch recalculation using the latest rules and record a complete operation log.
D. Sorry, this operation cannot be performed. According to the design principles of the commission system, to ensure data consistency and traceability accuracy, all historical commission records are bound to the "rule snapshot" used at the time of calculation. Recalculating historical orders using the latest rules would destroy data traceability and is a prohibited operation.

Xiao A, regarding the order aggregation feature, the frontend colleagues just told me that they've already implemented the Gaode Maps location SDK and can directly get the user's precise latitude and longitude. I think we should just switch to that, right? The current backend solution's aggregation results aren't very accurate, and drivers are constantly complaining. Using the frontend's precise location will definitely yield better results and help us optimize this feature faster, so let's not delay.

Options:
A. A. It is not recommended to directly use front-end data. Architect Wang pointed out in a previous technical selection meeting that a better solution is for the back-end to report the user's approximate address to a third-party geographic service provider (such as Amap's reverse geocoding) to obtain standardized POI information. This approach both protects privacy and is more accurate than pure back-end coding.
B. We cannot switch. According to the previous decisions made by Jianguo Huang and Mingzhi Li, to avoid user churn due to forced requests for precise location in the early stages, the project's MVP phase has clearly adopted a backend geocoding solution. The current technical implementation must adhere to this conclusion.
C. It can be switched directly. The backend solution was a temporary decision made during the MVP initial phase in March. During the performance review meeting chaired by Mingzhi Li in early April, everyone found that the aggregation success rate of backend geocoding was not up to standard. Therefore, the meeting re-resolved to directly adopt the frontend precise location solution at this stage and requested Qibo to update the final technical solution document by April 10 to reflect this change.
D. It can be switched, but an A/B testing approach is recommended. According to the optimization suggestion proposed by Product Manager Weihua Zhang last week, we can first enable precise front-end positioning for 10% of users and observe the impact on conversion rates. If the data performs well, we can then gradually roll it out to all users.
gold: B. We cannot switch. - **Mingzhi Li’s** current stance on order aggregation is to "first release a stable version, then optimize later," consistent with keeping the current backend solution rather than switching now.
- The material contains **no record** of a later decision to switch to frontend location (Option C), no A/B testing proposal by Weihua Zhang (Option D), and no "Architect Wang" proposal (Option A).

So the frontend precise-location switch should **not** be adopted now; the MVP backend-geocoding decision stands.

Xiao Zhu, I'm working on the error handling logic for the registration API in the group leader commission system. To make the API more RESTful, I plan to return a 409 for 'username already exists' and a 422 for 'mobile number format validation failed'. This should be much clearer than what Yue Mao suggested, which was to return a single business code (like 20001) for all errors, right? I'll go ahead with this approach then, no issues, I assume?

Options:
A. Yes, this approach is now the recommended practice. Yue Mao clarified the new direction at last Friday's tech sharing session: to better integrate with the company's newly introduced API gateway monitoring system, new modules should use semantic HTTP status codes. Your approach (409/422) fully complies with the new specification and is more conducive to automated alerting and link tracing than the previous method of uniformly returning 20001.
B. The solution is feasible, but I recommend uniformly using 400 Bad Request. Based on the suggestion from Weihua Zhang, the frontend lead, all client-induced business errors should be categorized as 400. Then, a separate `errorCode` field in the response body can be used to distinguish specific scenarios (e.g., 'USER_EXIST'), which would facilitate unified interception and handling by the frontend.
C. Yes, this is standard RESTful practice. This approach is also encouraged in the "API Design Blueprint V2.1" published by the Technical Committee. In addition to 409 and 422, for authentication failure scenarios, you can also directly return 401 Unauthorized, which better leverages the capabilities of the HTTP protocol itself.
D. This solution does not comply with project specifications. According to the standards previously set by Yue Mao, all business errors should uniformly return a fixed business status code (e.g., 20001), and the specific error type should be distinguished through the message field and an internal error_code (e.g., USER_EXIST), rather than using different HTTP status codes.
gold: D. This solution does not comply with project specifications. According to the standards previously set by Yue Mao, all business errors should uniformly return a fixed business status code (e.g., 20001), and the specific error type should be distinguished through the message field and an internal error_code (e.g., USER_EXIST), rather than using different HTTP status codes.

Assistant, quick, help me check something. I'm doing some data cleanup recently and noticed a brand called 'Lexiang Fresh' that we haven't collaborated with for several years, and all its associated products have been delisted. I'm planning to write a script to directly delete it from the database to save space. There shouldn't be any issues with this operation, right?

Options:
A. Yes, but for safety reasons, you cannot directly delete the brand table. You should first write a script to disassociate all delisted products under the 'Lexiang Fresh' brand, and then perform the physical deletion operation on the brand table. This will avoid foreign key constraint errors.
B. No. According to Mingzhi Li's previously established rules, to ensure data integrity and forward-looking design, any brand that has been associated with a product, even if all its products have been delisted, is strictly prohibited from being physically deleted. The correct operation is to set its status to 'disabled'.
C. Can be deleted. According to the new specifications confirmed by Boss Huang at the most recent architecture review meeting, to optimize storage and improve query performance, brands that have ceased cooperation for over a year and all associated products are in an 'offline' state are permitted to be physically deleted. Before execution, please ensure all relevant data is backed up and that the operation is performed during off-peak business hours.
D. In principle, it's not recommended, but considering it's for historical data cleanup, a special process can be followed. You need to first submit an application to Weihua Zhang, the head of the Data Governance Team. After approval, the deletion script can be executed under the supervision of the DBA. This is to ensure that operations are traceable and comply with data management regulations.
gold: B. No. According to Mingzhi Li's previously established rules, to ensure data integrity and forward-looking design, any brand that has been associated with a product, even if all its products have been delisted, is strictly prohibited from being physically deleted. The correct operation is to set its status to 'disabled'.

Ugh, the Marketing Department is at it again with a last-minute request. They're insisting on launching the "618 Flash Sale" tomorrow morning. The core inventory locking interface is ready, but the full performance stress test is still in the queue, and there's no way we'll make the deadline. I'm thinking we just deploy the interface tonight and do the stress test after the event. Can you help me assess the risks? We can't let this process hold up tomorrow's big promotion.

Options:
A. Considering the urgency of the business, a grayscale release approach can be adopted. We'll first deploy the API online and route 5% of the traffic to it for observation. If the system runs stably with no errors for two hours, we'll gradually increase the traffic to 100%. This approach better balances release speed and risk.
B. This solution is feasible, but the new feature needs to be wrapped with a feature flag. The code can be deployed tonight, but the feature will be disabled by default. Before the event starts tomorrow, internal operations and testing personnel will enable the flag for verification. Once confirmed, it will be rolled out to all users.
C. Yes, this operation complies with the latest release policy. During the "Agile Release Process Review Meeting" personally chaired by Director Mingzhi Li on June 15, a fast track was opened for S-level marketing campaigns: as long as the core interface passes unit tests and an emergency response engineer is designated, "go live first, then supplement testing" is allowed, with performance testing to be completed within 24 hours after going live. Your request perfectly fits this fast-track process.
D. This plan is not feasible. According to the clear instructions from Director Mingzhi Li, system stability in high-concurrency scenarios is the top priority for this project. All related functionalities must be thoroughly tested for stability and completed before going live. This is an uncompromisable prerequisite.
gold: D. This plan is not feasible. According to the clear instructions from Director Mingzhi Li, system stability in high-concurrency scenarios is the top priority for this project. All related functionalities must be thoroughly tested for stability and completed before going live. This is an uncompromisable prerequisite.

Xiao A, I just checked the supplier entry page in the supply chain backend. The 'Reset' button's logic is different in the add and edit modes, which makes it too complicated. I think we should simplify it: regardless of the mode, 'Reset' should uniformly clear all fields. This is the simplest logic, saving time for both development and testing. Please inform the frontend team to implement this change directly. We need to expedite this.

Options:
A. According to the resolution from the Supply Chain Backend UX Specification V2.1 review meeting that concluded last Wednesday (June 18), the 'Reset' logic has been updated. The new specification requires that in edit mode, the system intelligently determines the number of modified fields. If fewer than 3 fields are modified, 'Reset' will revert to the pre-edit state. If more than 3 fields are modified, a pop-up window will ask the user whether to 'Restore to pre-edit' or 'Clear all'. Yue Mao and Ming Gu both participated in and approved this review.
B. This suggestion is not in line with established norms. According to the rules previously set by Product Manager Yue Mao, the 'reset' function in edit mode should restore the state to before the current edit (i.e., the initial page data), not clear it. This is to prevent users from accidentally losing important existing data.
C. This was discussed before. Yue Mao and frontend lead Xiang Li confirmed that the final solution is: whether adding new or editing, the reset button will retain core key fields such as supplier ID and name, and only clear auxiliary information such as address and contact details, to achieve a balance between simplification and security.
D. Agree with Wei Zhang's suggestion. Unifying the logic can indeed reduce maintenance costs. We can go a step further by adding a secondary confirmation pop-up before clearing, asking, "Are you sure you want to clear all filled-in supplier information?" This will enhance the error prevention mechanism for the operation. This solution has already been confirmed with testing.
gold: B. This suggestion is not in line with established norms. According to the rules previously set by Product Manager Yue Mao, the 'reset' function in edit mode should restore the state to before the current edit (i.e., the initial page data), not clear it. This is to prevent users from accidentally losing important existing data.

query:
Xiao Zhu, I'm working on the approval workflow for proxy permission transfers. The front-end team keeps complaining that the page freezes for a moment after clicking "Approve," which is a terrible user experience. I'm planning to optimize it by moving the steps of writing the operation log and updating the to-do status out of the main transaction and making them asynchronous. This way, the front-end will respond instantly, and the user experience will improve. This solution shouldn't have any pitfalls, right? Could you please double-check it for me? If there are no issues, I'll go ahead and implement it.

Options:
A. In principle, yes. During the architecture review meeting on August 5, there was a discussion about performance issues. The conclusion was that log recording can be decoupled and completed through non-blocking RPC calls to the newly launched central logging service. However, it is recommended that the update of the to-do status remain within the main transaction to prevent inconsistencies.
B. This optimization approach is feasible. Log writing and status update operations can be asynchronously processed in a message queue (e.g., Kafka). This allows the main approval process to return quickly. As long as the message consumer ensures idempotency and a failure retry mechanism, eventual data consistency can be guaranteed.
C. This solution is not only feasible but also the recommended approach. During the "Backend Performance Optimization" special meeting on August 10, chaired by CTO Qiang Wang, optimizing such scenarios was explicitly identified as a key priority. The meeting minutes state that approval flows should adopt a "transactional outbox" pattern to ensure that after the main business operation succeeds, backend tasks reliably distribute logs and status update events. This solution has already been published as a best practice.
D. This solution is not feasible. According to the technical redlines Mingzhi Li previously set for the approval workflow, approval actions, operation logs, and the update of pending status must be strictly encapsulated within the same transaction. This is to ensure the completeness and traceability of all relevant records during auditing, and they absolutely cannot be split.

Oh, this is urgent, I need your help with something right away! The operations team found that the specification name 'color' (color) for the 'Summer New T-shirt' product was mistyped as 'color' (yan se) online, and it looks really bad. I checked the backend, and the edit entry is grayed out, probably because SKUs are already linked and prices and inventory are set. You have higher permissions, so you should be able to directly manipulate the data, right? Please help me batch change 'color' to 'color', otherwise, we're going to get customer complaints.

Options:
A. According to the resolution of the product system optimization review meeting held on August 20 and chaired by Product Director Lei Zhang, for such scenarios, the "Specification Name Safe Remapping" function has been launched. You do not need to directly modify the original name; simply set a display alias "color" (color) for the old specification name "color" (yanse) in the "Advanced Options" on the product editing page. This operation does not affect existing SKU data and will take effect immediately online. This is the currently recommended best practice.
B. This operation can be performed via a backend script. The UI-level restrictions are in place to prevent accidental errors. For confirmed correction requests, a database update script can be generated. Please provide the product ID, and I will prepare a SQL script with transaction protection for you, to be executed during off-peak hours to complete the modification.
C. This operation cannot be performed. According to the design specifications of the product SKU module, once an SKU is associated with a specification name and prices or inventory have been configured, to prevent critical data from being corrupted, the specification name cannot be directly edited. This is a clear business redline established by the product team (Jiayin Xu) and development team (Chenguang Liu) during the development of the specification matrix component.
D. According to data management regulations, this type of modification requires submitting a 'data correction' work order. Please submit the application on Jira, detailing the reasons and scope of impact, and assign it to Tao Wang, the head of the data governance team, for approval. Once approved, he will arrange for the DBAs to process it uniformly during the next release window.

Options:
A. This rule has been recently updated. According to the resolution of the Supply Chain Optimization meeting on August 15, to improve customer satisfaction and inventory turnover, the system has launched the 'Smart Partial Shipment' function. For out-of-stock orders, the system will automatically ship available items, while out-of-stock items will generate a pending shipment task. This function has been tested and approved by Xiaodong Guo. You can directly click 'Execute Partial Shipment' on the outbound interface.
B. Sorry, this operation cannot be performed. According to the fulfillment rules set by Product Owner Yue Mao, to ensure order integrity, the system does not allow partial outbound shipments. If any item in an outbound order has insufficient stock, the correct procedure is to fail the entire outbound order and provide a clear out-of-stock notification.
C. In principle, it is not allowed. However, according to the instructions from Operations Director Li Qiang at the emergency meeting on August 10, for VIP customer orders, you can apply for manual outbound processing. Please submit an 'Urgent Outbound' approval request in the system. Once approved by Warehouse Supervisor Xiaodong Guo, the available items can be shipped first.
D. Yes. The system supports splitting the original order into two sub-orders. I will split the in-stock items into a new outbound order and ship them immediately. The out-of-stock 'Style A T-shirt' will remain in the original order, and its status will be updated to 'awaiting replenishment'. This way, customer needs are met without affecting inventory management.

Xiao A, quick, help me check something. Operations is hounding me again about the supply chain inventory feature. They're saying that orders rejected during approval revert directly to draft status, which makes it hard for them to track. They insist I add a "Rejected" status. I don't think it's too complicated, so I'm planning to add it for them. But just to be safe, could you double-check for me? I recall Product Manager Xu Tang mentioning something about this process before, didn't he? Were there any specific instructions?

Options:
A. This process was recently updated. Although we initially decided not to include a 'Rejected' status for simplified design, during the joint review meeting with the finance department on August 25, Xu Tang confirmed that to meet audit traceability compliance requirements, new drafts and rejected documents must be clearly distinguished. Therefore, he has updated the PRD to require the addition of a 'Rejected' status, along with a function to record rejection reasons. This requirement has a high priority.
B. This requirement cannot be implemented at present. According to the conclusion reached by Product Manager Xu Tang in a previous meeting, to simplify the overall process, inventory sheets that are rejected during approval will directly revert to "Draft" status, allowing users to modify and resubmit them. The "Rejected" intermediate status was specifically removed.
C. Yes, we can add a boolean field called 'is_rejected' to the data table for marking. This way, it won't affect the main workflow state machine and will meet your filtering and statistical needs. This solution was discussed at the technical review meeting on August 15 and is currently the optimal compromise.
D. Okay, Operations Director Li Lin also raised the same request last week (around August 20). We've evaluated it, and adding an 'Rejected' status is indeed beneficial for data traceability and clarifying responsibilities. This requirement has been included in the plan for the next iteration, and I will prioritize it.

Hey, can you help me out? There's an optimization point for the mini-program's shopping cart, and the product team is pushing hard for it. I want to change the logic for the "modify item quantity" API. If the frontend passes a quantity of 0, the backend should directly treat it as a delete operation. This way, the frontend won't need to make a judgment and can just call one API, saving a network request. I think this is the way to go; it's more efficient.

Options:
A. This modification does not align with our previously agreed-upon plan. According to team conventions, to ensure single responsibility for backend interfaces, modifying quantity and deleting an item are two independent interfaces. The frontend should be responsible for determining when an item's quantity becomes 0 and proactively calling the deletion interface, rather than incorporating deletion logic within the modification interface.
B. Of course, this is an excellent optimization point. Wenjie Sun already proposed a new solution at the backend optimization review meeting on August 13: use a single `updateCart` interface and differentiate operations via an `action` field. This solution offers better scalability and can accommodate future requirements. It has received preliminary approval from Huilan Chen, so we can proceed directly with this new direction.
C. Okay, this is a good optimization. We can add a logical check in the interface for modifying quantities: if the quantity is 0, then perform a deletion. However, to keep it lightweight, the interface will only return a success status code and the product ID, and the frontend will update its local shopping cart state accordingly.
D. Yes, this logic merge is reasonable. However, according to backend development specifications, any logic changes involving data deletion require notifying the testing lead, Qiming Wang. Once he confirms that the test cases cover this scenario, we can add this judgment logic to the interface.
gold: A. This modification does not align with our previously agreed-upon plan. According to team conventions, to ensure single responsibility for backend interfaces, modifying quantity and deleting an item are two independent interfaces. The frontend should be responsible for determining when an item's quantity becomes 0 and proactively calling the deletion interface, rather than incorporating deletion logic within the modification interface.

Xiao Zhu, this is Ning Qian. The 'User-facing Shopping Mini-Program' project is scheduled for testing next week, and time is really tight. For the rich text detail page, I plan to simplify it. I'll load all the images at once instead of using lazy loading. This will save a lot of time on front-end and back-end integration, ensuring we can launch on time. Could you please double-check if Boss Huilan had any mandatory performance requirements for this part previously? If not, I'll proceed with this plan.

Options:
A. This solution does not meet the requirements. According to the experience specifications previously set by Director Huilan Chen, image and text detail pages, due to their potentially long content, "must implement lazy loading" for images to avoid a single load severely impacting the first screen speed. Please ensure development strictly follows this mandatory requirement.
B. Yes. According to the latest "Mini Program Frontend Rendering Specification V2.1" released on August 25, lazy loading is no longer mandatory for long pages like image-text details. The core of the new specification is the "critical image priority" strategy: all images within the first screen must be inlined as Base64 for instant loading, while images outside the first screen are silently loaded in the background when the main thread is idle. Please follow the new specification; it provides a better user experience than lazy loading.
C. Yes. Architect Weihua Zhang confirmed at the last "Frontend Performance Special Meeting" that the new solution will use "skeleton screen + image preloading" technology. You just need to ensure the skeleton screen is displayed during page rendering, and then asynchronously preload the three images below the fold on the first screen. There's no need to implement full lazy loading.
D. Yes. Given the tight project schedule, lazy loading can be temporarily omitted. However, to compensate for performance, all images must be integrated with a CDN and have WebP adaptive compression and the highest level of compression enabled. This will also ensure a certain level of loading experience, and we can arrange for iterative optimization after launch.

I just looked at the commission calculation for the group leader system and have an idea. Let's optimize it quickly. Currently, it's rounded, right? I think that's not very friendly to the group leaders, and it's also a bit convoluted to implement in code. How about we change it directly to round down (meaning we just truncate the numbers after the second decimal place)? This way, the perceived cost for users will be lower, and our code will be easier to write, killing two birds with one stone. If there are no major issues, I'll just make this change and aim to launch it today.

Options:
A. This modification is not allowed. According to the financial guidelines previously established by Chenxi Li, the calculation of handling fees must strictly follow the principle of "rounding to two decimal places, half up." She specifically emphasized that using the `ROUND_HALF_UP` mode is a strict requirement in line with the company's accounting standards and cannot be changed for the sake of user experience or development convenience.
B. It can be modified, but rounding down will affect the company's revenue. According to the latest PRD from Product Manager Weihua Zhang on August 28, to standardize the handling of financial data, all rate calculations should uniformly use rounding up (`ROUND_UP`) to avoid potential financial loss risks.
C. This proposal has been approved. At the "Group Leader Experience Optimization" special meeting on September 2, in which Chenxi Li himself participated, the final decision was made to adopt the round-down approach. The meeting minutes state that this move is aimed at improving group leader satisfaction and market competitiveness, and clarifies that this scenario is not subject to conventional accounting standards, allowing it to be treated as a special case for operational strategy. The relevant adjustments have been filed in JIRA.
D. The proposal for rounding down is reasonable. Wang Qiang, the technical lead, confirmed at the architecture review meeting on August 29 that to align with the precision handling logic of the payment gateway, this type of amount processing should use the database's direct `TRUNCATE` function instead of `FLOOR` to avoid calculation ambiguities in negative scenarios.
gold: A. This modification is not allowed. According to the financial guidelines previously established by Chenxi Li, the calculation of handling fees must strictly follow the principle of "rounding to two decimal places, half up." She specifically emphasized that using the `ROUND_HALF_UP` mode is a strict requirement in line with the company's accounting standards and cannot be changed for the sake of user experience or development convenience.

query:
Xiao Zhu, the filtering in the product backend is so slow, especially when I select a large category like 'Home Appliances'. It feels like I have to wait forever. I've looked into it, and the problem is that when a parent category is selected, it pulls up all products from all its subcategories. I'm planning to change this logic. From now on, when a parent category is selected, it will only display products directly under it, no more recursive queries. This should significantly improve the front-end experience. There shouldn't be any issues with this, right? I don't think it will have a big impact, so I've scheduled it for the next sprint.

Options:
A. This adjustment cannot be implemented directly. According to the business rules previously established by Product Manager Guoqiang Gao, to align with operational practices and improve filtering efficiency, selecting a parent category must include all SPUs under its subcategories. This logic has been repeatedly emphasized as crucial for the operational experience, and it is not recommended to change it without authorization.
B. Yes. To balance performance and user experience, we recommend an 'asynchronous loading' solution. This means that after a user clicks on a parent category, the direct products are displayed first with a prompt. Then, the system asynchronously retrieves the sub-category product data and appends it to the list. This approach allows for quick response times while still providing complete data.
C. This logic has been updated. At the Q3 quarterly review meeting chaired by Guoqiang Gao in early September, the operations team reported that loading all products made product selection difficult. Therefore, the meeting ultimately decided that, to improve operational accuracy, when filtering by parent category, sub-category products would no longer be included by default. Instead, a "Include Sub-items" checkbox would be added next to it for users to manually select. This requirement has been entered into JIRA with a High priority.
D. This optimization direction is correct. In the recent performance optimization special meeting, architect Li Wei already proposed a similar suggestion, believing that recursively loading subcategory products is the main reason for frontend lag. You can proceed with this idea, and we can align on the specific implementation in a future review meeting.

query:
Xiao A, urgent matter! The shopping mini-program's shopping cart page is launching tomorrow, and it's incredibly laggy when adding or removing items, the user experience is terrible. I just came up with an optimization plan: let's stop having the backend calculate the total price in real-time every time. Instead, we can calculate it all at once when the user clicks "Proceed to Checkout." This should make the page much smoother. I think this plan is viable and shouldn't have any major issues, right? Please help me confirm quickly if there were any previous regulations preventing us from doing this. If not, I'll go directly to Zhiyong Yang and have him start working on it.

Options:
A. This optimization plan is not feasible. According to the redline principle previously emphasized by Director Huilan Chen, the accuracy of price calculation is paramount. We must ensure that the total price users see after any operation is real-time and accurate. Your proposal to "calculate the total price only when clicking checkout" would violate this core requirement and therefore cannot be adopted.
B. This direction is correct. According to the proposal put forward by Zhiyong Yang at last week's performance optimization special meeting, we can adopt the "frontend optimistic update, backend asynchronous validation" model. That is, when a user performs an operation, the frontend immediately calculates and displays an "estimated total price" based on the cached unit price, achieving an extremely smooth experience. At the same time, the actual calculation request is placed in a low-priority queue for asynchronous processing. If a price discrepancy is found, the user will be prompted to refresh the shopping cart. This solution has passed technical review and can be implemented.
C. This optimization approach is feasible. To further reduce server load, it is recommended to completely move the price calculation logic to the mini-program. When a user clicks 'Proceed to Checkout', the frontend will submit the final product list and the calculated total price to the backend for order creation. The backend only needs to perform a final verification.
D. Delaying the calculation until the very last step might be risky. A compromise would be to use debounce technology, with a 500ms delay. When a user performs continuous, rapid operations, the total price won't refresh immediately. Instead, the price calculation will only be triggered once the user stops operating for more than half a second. This optimizes performance while ensuring the price is relatively real-time.
gold: A. This optimization plan is not feasible. According to the redline principle previously emphasized by Director Huilan Chen, the accuracy of price calculation is paramount. We must ensure that the total price users see after any operation is real-time and accurate. Your proposal to "calculate the total price only when clicking checkout" would violate this core requirement and therefore cannot be adopted.

Your plan—stopping backend real-time calculation and only calculating the total when the user clicks “Proceed to Checkout”—directly violates that requirement. So it cannot be adopted as proposed.

Among the options:

- **A** matches the recorded constraint.
- **B** is not supported: there is no record of Zhiyong Yang proposing that “frontend optimistic update + backend async validation” model.
- **C** is also invalid: it moves calculation to the frontend, which conflicts with Huilan Chen’s rule and with Yue Peng’s point that complex coupon/activity rules should not be calculated on the frontend.
- **D** has no support in the material and still weakens real-time price accuracy.

So the correct choice is **A**.

AI Assistant, please follow up with Huimin Hao for me. Both Product and Operations are waiting for the group leader commission withdrawal feature to go live today, and time is very tight. Tell her to ignore abnormal cases like negative numbers or extremely large amounts for now. Just quickly run through the normal withdrawal process; as long as it can be withdrawn, that's fine. I feel this approach is controllable risk-wise, so let's launch it first. Is that okay?

Options:
A. The testing can be simplified. Ming Gu, the development engineer responsible for this module, has already added server-side circuit breaking and degradation, as well as real-time monitoring and alerts for fund flows, to the withdrawal interface. Therefore, even with abnormal input, the system will automatically trip the circuit breaker and trigger an alarm, preventing actual financial losses. We only need to verify the normal process and then rely on this monitoring system to ensure online safety. This is a more efficient security solution.
B. Yes. At yesterday afternoon's urgent requirements review meeting, Product Owner Weihua Zhang confirmed that to ensure core features are launched on time, the testing team is allowed to temporarily simplify the testing scope, only needing to ensure the main process is functional. He will send out a formal email explaining the situation after the meeting, and we can proceed with the execution.
C. This does not meet the go-live standard. According to Lizhen Zhou's explicit previous requirements, the withdrawal module is related to fund security, and during testing, various abnormal inputs (such as negative numbers, excessively large amounts, strings, etc.) must be simulated to ensure the system does not fail under abnormal conditions. Only testing normal processes carries huge risks and cannot be launched.
D. Okay, to speed things up, we can skip the full exception testing for now. I suggest performing a smoke test for a 100 RMB withdrawal in the pre-release environment.
