I (Ting Ye) attended the cross-departmental discussion on "incentivizing group leaders." The product and tech teams had a very in-depth discussion. After the meeting, Director Xiaofeng Wu approached me and said, "You should also think about this and see how we can more effectively incentivize group leaders." How should I present my suggestions to him?

Options:
A. Boss Wu, from the perspective of industry best practices in operations, I suggest we change our approach. Since the latest technical solution is to switch to pushing "Group Leader Performance Weekly Reports" via email, our marketing department should take the lead in designing and operating this weekly report. For example, we can design an exquisite weekly report template, use Mailchimp for personalized pushes, and create more attractive titles, such as "XX, congratulations on outperforming 80% of group leaders last week!" In terms of content, in addition to core data, we can also add sections like "This Week's Dark Horse Product Recommendations" or "Top-Selling Group Leader Experience Sharing" to make it a valuable information source that group leaders look forward to every week.
B. Boss Wu, I believe the real-time order inquiry feature that the tech team is developing is an excellent incentive tool in itself. Our marketing department can plan a series of content marketing activities around it, such as writing a strategy article titled "Mastering the New Backend, Easily Viewing Earnings," and launching a "Share Your First Order" check-in activity in the group leader communities. We can offer additional rewards to group leaders who share screenshots of their use of the new feature, turning a product function into a successful marketing incentive event.
C. Boss Wu, to implement the "Leader Performance Weekly Report" solution, we need to set up a Cron Job that executes every Monday at midnight. This task will batch calculate each leader's performance and ranking from the previous week and aggregate the results into a dedicated weekly report data table. Then, the system will call the email gateway service, read the HTML template and data, and push it in batches to all leaders. To avoid duplicate calculations, we also need to record the execution status and timestamp of each run in the task table.
D. Boss Wu, I believe the core of the incentive lies in providing a highly available data interface. We need to ensure that this API supports filtering by order status and time range, and defaults to sorting by creation time in descending order. The returned fields must be comprehensive, including `product_image`, `order_amount`, and `final_commission`. Most critically, the `commission_status` field must be strictly aligned with the settlement system.
gold: B. Boss Wu, I believe the real-time order inquiry feature that the tech team is developing is an excellent incentive tool in itself. The project team has just finalized the selection of the payment gateway, and I (Wenjie Sun) have been assigned to handle the subsequent technical integration and development work. Our project's core is a social e-commerce model centered around 'Group Leaders'. A major pain point currently reported by operations is that the commission settlement process for Group Leaders is cumbersome and slow, which affects their motivation. Now, my leader has asked me to design a technical implementation plan for fast and accurate commission distribution based on the new payment solution. How should I present this plan to the team?

Options:
A. Since the team has decided to adopt Company C's solution, its API inherently supports real-time ledger splitting. My proposal is to directly leverage this capability: 1. Upon receiving the payment success callback notification, the business system immediately calculates the commission amount based on the order information. 2. Subsequently, it synchronously calls the ledger splitting interface provided by Company C to transfer the specified amount from the main merchant account to the team leader's secondary merchant virtual account. Since ledger splitting is critical to the core business closed loop, and the API responds quickly, synchronous calls can simplify the process and ensure real-time performance. 3. To ensure data consistency, the entire process (updating local order status, recording ledger splitting details, calling external APIs) will be encapsulated within Spring's `@Transactional` annotation to ensure atomicity of operations.
B. Based on the latest resolution from the architecture review meeting on February 21, we need to develop our own ledger system. My proposal will be based on our existing Java technology stack: 1. After a user successfully pays, the main business system will only send an MQ message containing order and commission information to RabbitMQ and then immediately respond, ensuring high performance and low latency for the main payment process. 2. Create an independent ledger service (built with Spring Boot) to act as the consumer for this MQ. After receiving the message, the service will execute complex ledger logic, such as calculating dynamic commissions based on team leader levels. 3. When updating a team leader's account balance, to prevent concurrent update errors, I will use database pessimistic locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) to lock the account row, ensuring the atomicity of balance calculation and update. 4. At the same time, establish an independent reconciliation mechanism to regularly compare with the original bills from the payment gateway daily, ensuring the accuracy of calculations made by the self-developed system.
C. Based on the decision to develop an in-house ledger splitting system, using Go would be the most efficient choice. My proposal is as follows: 1. After a successful payment, the main service will send ledger splitting tasks in real-time to a dedicated ledger splitting microservice via gRPC, achieving efficient inter-service communication. 2. Within the ledger splitting service, a memory queue protected by `sync.Mutex` will be used to buffer sudden requests, and a Goroutine pool will be launched to process these tasks in parallel. 3. For updating account balances, I would choose to use Redis's `INCRBYFLOAT` atomic operation, which is orders of magnitude faster than operating on a database and can easily support high-concurrency ledger splitting requests. 4. The entire service can be compiled into a statically linked binary, packaged into an Alpine Docker image smaller than 20MB, enabling extremely fast deployment and elastic scaling.
D. Company C's real-time ledger splitting API performs well. My solution is: 1. After a successful payment callback, encapsulate the ledger splitting task (e.g., order ID, splitting rules) into a message and deliver it to an internal Channel. 2. Start a Goroutine pool as consumers to concurrently retrieve tasks from the Channel and call Company C's ledger splitting API. 3. This decouples the ledger splitting operation from the main business logic after a successful payment, preventing potential delays from the ledger splitting API from affecting the performance of the entire callback processing chain, and significantly improves system throughput through concurrency.

As the Product Manager, I (Guoqiang Gao) am leading the optimization of the payment gateway's disbursement function. The core pain points currently are inconsistent data during financial reconciliation and a chaotic process for handling failed orders. To prepare for the technical review, how should I articulate the core points of the product requirements?

Options:
A. I would suggest from a technical implementation perspective, the specific implementation ideas could be: 1. The core PayoutService method must be annotated with `@Transactional(propagation = Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW)` to ensure that each payout operation runs in an independent transaction, avoiding large transaction issues. 2. The retry logic is recommended to be implemented using a message queue (e.g., RabbitMQ)'s delayed queue, which is more robust than `@Async` plus `Thread.sleep` and will not occupy thread pool resources for a long time. 3. After retry attempts are exhausted, update the transaction status to `PAYOUT_FAILED` and publish a `PayoutFailedEvent` domain event, which will be asynchronously listened to by a dedicated `NotificationEventListener` to call the notification center RPC interface.
B. From an implementation perspective, this adjustment can significantly simplify the backend's core transaction logic. All retry and asynchronous code can be removed from the PayoutService methods called by the Controller. 1. We only need to catch all `Exceptions` within the `try-catch` block when calling the third-party gateway, and then update the corresponding transaction status in the database to `MANUAL_PENDING`. 2. The next focus is to develop a completely new backend management API, primarily including: a `GET /api/payouts/failures` interface for the finance backend that supports multi-condition filtering and pagination, and a core `POST /api/payouts/{id}/retry` manual retry interface, which requires strict permission and status validation internally.
C. I will first share an important piece of information: According to the direction finalized by CTO Mingzhi Li at yesterday's architecture meeting, we must adjust our product strategy, prioritizing "ultimate stability and clear responsibilities." Therefore, my proposal will focus on: 1. "Simplifying the transaction process": The backend's calls to payment channels will strictly adhere to the "single attempt principle." Any failure (regardless of the reason) will immediately be routed to a "pending manual review" status, completely eliminating the risk of data inconsistency that automatic retries might cause. 2. "Empowering financial operations": The R&D focus will shift to building a "payment anomaly handling center" for the finance team, providing functionalities such as querying failed lists, tracing transaction details, and granting operational permissions for "manual retry" or "mark as closed." 3. "Strengthening risk control and auditing": All manual intervention operations must record the operator, operation time, and reason remarks, forming a complete audit log to meet compliance requirements. Although this solution temporarily increases the manual cost for the finance department, it maximizes system stability and fund security, making it the optimal solution at this stage.
D. I would emphasize that the core of the product solution is to ensure data integrity and process certainty. Specifically: 1. "Define a complete payment state machine": Clearly distinguish between 'in progress', 'system error (retryable)', and 'business failure (final state)' to ensure states do not drift. 2. "Design an idempotent automatic retry mechanism": For system errors, implement automatic retries with increasing delays and set a reasonable maximum number of attempts to prevent infinite retries. 3. "Establish full-link audit logs": All key requests, responses, and state changes must be persisted to provide undeniable reconciliation and problem traceability. 4. "Achieve a closed loop for failure handling": For ultimately failed orders, an alert must be triggered and a work order automatically created to ensure the finance team can intervene promptly and without omissions.

I'm Fang Wang, a Senior Engineer from another business line. Recently, I was invited to give a technical presentation to a sister team on how to handle data consistency issues under high concurrency. They are currently experiencing occasional inconsistencies in critical data (like inventory) during promotional events. To make my presentation practical, which validated solution from our team should I focus on as the most recommendable? Please help me outline a presentation plan.

Options:
A. The core experience is to manually implement atomic operations based on Redis. The steps of 'reading current inventory, checking if sufficient, and performing deduction' can be encapsulated into a Lua script, and then executed on the Redis server via the `EVAL` command. Because Redis executes Lua scripts in a single thread, this fundamentally eliminates concurrent competition and ensures data consistency. This solution offers high performance, does not rely on any third-party libraries, and has very clear implementation logic.
B. I suggest focusing on our solution using the Redisson client. We can introduce it as follows: For business scenarios requiring strong consistency (e.g., product inventory), we acquire a distributed lock (RLock) for each resource (e.g., product ID). All read-modify-write operations are executed within a `try-finally` block, ensuring the lock is released in the `finally` block. Redisson not only encapsulates Lua-based atomic operations but also provides a watchdog mechanism to automatically extend lock leases. This is a mature solution in our technology stack for handling such problems, effectively preventing deadlocks, and is more reliable and easier to promote than manually writing and maintaining Lua scripts.
C. Considering the simplification of the technology stack and avoiding the potential complexity of distributed locks, I recommend following the standard practice recently established by the company's Architecture Committee at the Q2 review meeting: using database-level optimistic locking. Specifically, a field with the `@Version` annotation can be added to the JPA entity class of the inventory table. The business code does not need any manual locking; it can simply modify and save the entity as usual. When concurrent updates occur, JPA will automatically detect version conflicts and throw an `OptimisticLockException`. The upper-layer service will then catch this exception and perform a retry. This solution pushes concurrency control down to the database, which is currently the more favored approach.
D. In fact, for scenarios with extremely high consistency requirements, the Architecture Committee also recommended the database pessimistic locking solution. The idea is that after a transaction starts, it queries the inventory record using a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` statement, which locks that row of data until the transaction is committed or rolled back. Any other transaction attempting to modify that row will be blocked and wait. Although this reduces some concurrency, it can completely prevent concurrent modifications at a mechanistic level, achieving the strongest level of consistency guarantee, and the code logic is simpler than handling the retry mechanism of optimistic locking.

Based on the team's actual track record, the **most recommendable validated solution is B — the Redisson distributed lock (RLock)**.

Why this one is "validated" and the others aren't:

- **Minghui Zou** completed the manual order cancellation interface and its concurrency test **passed using a Redisson distributed lock** — this is the team's concrete, proven result for exactly the kind of high-concurrency inventory-deduction scenario your sister team is facing.
- **Mingzhi Li** (the technical lead) endorsed this direction: Redis distributed locks are the conventional solution, with attention to reasonable lock timeout and releasing the lock in a `finally` block to avoid deadlocks, and suggested Lua scripts to guarantee atomicity — which Redisson natively encapsulates.
- **Huilan Chen** praised Minghui Zou for resolving the concurrency issue and removing the core risk, confirming the approach worked in practice.
- **You (Fang Wang)** are already planning to use distributed locks for hot data in your caching architecture, so this is consistent with your own design direction.

The other options are weaker as recommendations from your team's evidence:

- **A (manual Redis Lua script via EVAL)**: the underlying atomicity idea is sound and was discussed, but the team's *final validated* implementation went through **Redisson**, not a hand-rolled script. Manual scripts are harder to maintain — Redisson already wraps the Lua atomic operations.
- **C (JPA `@Version` optimistic locking) and D (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`)**: these are presented as "Architecture Committee" recommendations, but there is **no evidence in the team's records** that the committee actually endorsed these, nor that either was validated in this team's experience. They don't belong in the "our validated solution" slot.

---

### Suggested presentation plan

1. **Problem statement (2 min)** — Inventory data consistency under high concurrency: lost updates, overselling, deadlocks.

2. **Recommended solution: Redisson distributed lock (10 min)**
   - Acquire an `RLock` per resource key (e.g., product ID).
   - Perform all read-modify-write operations inside a `try-finally` block, releasing the lock in `finally` to guarantee release.
   - Explain Redisson's **watchdog** auto-extension, which prevents the lock from expiring mid-operation under long GC pauses or slow business logic.
   - Note that Redisson internally uses **Lua-based atomic operations**, so you get the single-threaded Redis atomicity without maintaining custom scripts.
   - Set a reasonable lock timeout as a safety net.

3. **Evidence of validation from our team (5 min)**
   - Manual order cancellation interface: **concurrency test passed with Redisson distributed lock** (Minghui Zou).
   - Same pattern used for idempotency on the WeChat Pay callback interface with Redis locks — high-concurrency stress test stable, no race conditions found (Yue Peng).
   - Lead engineer guidance: conventional approach, pay attention to timeout + `finally` release to avoid deadlock (Mingzhi Li).

4. **Best practices & pitfalls (3 min)**
   - Always release in `finally`.
   - Lock timeout tuned to business execution time.
   - Use the watchdog for long-running operations.
   - Cover abnormal scenarios: network timeouts, service restarts (as instructed by Mingzhi Li).

5. **When NOT to use it (2 min)** — briefly compare with alternatives:
   - Pure manual Lua scripts: works, but more maintenance burden.
   - Optimistic locking (@Version): good for low contention, painful retry logic under heavy contention.
   - Pessimistic locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`): strongest guarantee but blocks and reduces throughput.

I (Liang Cheng) have just been brought in to get up to speed on the progress of a new mini-program project. The PM said that the product team has already produced a detailed design draft, defining all pages and core user paths. He hopes that, based on this design, I can proactively plan from my professional perspective to ensure the project's smooth launch and stable operation. How should I get started and propose an initial plan?

Options:
A. I will thoroughly analyze the user journey defined in the design document and translate it into key technical paths, such as "order placement API, payment callback, coupon distribution," etc. Subsequently, I will plan to use Prometheus to measure the QPS, latency, and error rate of these core APIs. At the Kubernetes level, I will configure appropriate resource requests and limits, as well as Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA) for the relevant services, and set corresponding alert thresholds to ensure the system's elasticity and stability during traffic peaks.
B. I will strictly adhere to CTO Mingzhi Li's resolution on technology stack unification from last week's Technical Committee meeting. First, I will plan to integrate Filebeat and Logstash into the mini-program's backend services to push all structured logs uniformly to the company's ELK cluster. Then, I will collaborate with the product manager to jointly define key business SLIs/SLOs (Service Level Indicators/Objectives) based on the design mockups and build a monitoring dashboard in Kibana. Finally, I will configure ElastAlert rules, such as "payment success rate below 99% within 5 minutes," to achieve real-time alerts for core business metrics and ensure business continuity.
C. I will first review Huilan Chen's design drafts on Figma, focusing on evaluating whether the core user journey from browsing products to completing payment is smooth and unobstructed. I will pay attention to the rationality of the information architecture and adopt Xiaofeng Wu's suggestion to strengthen the "Invite Friends" feature into an independent "Promotion Center" to optimize the sharing and referral path. At the same time, I will also propose adding an "Estimated Delivery Time" display on the order confirmation page and communicate with the backend team about its technical feasibility to enhance the overall user experience.
D. To support CTO Mingzhi Li's new specifications from last week's technical committee at the source, I suggest moving monitoring upstream to the design phase. I advocate for directly annotating embed event IDs and required reporting fields for each critical user interaction point (e.g., click to pay, share success) within Huilan Chen's Figma design mockups. This way, front-end development can precisely implement data collection based on the design mockups, ensuring high consistency in data format entering the ELK platform. This will lay a solid foundation for data quality for subsequent business indicator analysis and alert configuration.

Siyuan Qiu, Yuan Ji, and their team have finalized the preliminary plan for the mini-program's data tracking points. Now, the testing team needs to get involved to design a solution to ensure the accuracy of data reporting and to completely resolve issues like "user paid but no event received in the backend." If this task were assigned to you, how would you plan it?

Options:
A. Of course. I will strictly follow the strategy of "server-side validation first, client-side sampling as supplementary" emphasized by the CTO at the recent technical review meeting. According to the internal testing specifications released by the newly established "Data Quality Assurance Special Group," the current highest priority is to ensure the absolute reliability of the data reception service. Therefore, I will use JUnit to conduct in-depth testing of the service's API, covering not only conventional CRUD operations but also focusing on designing chaos engineering test scenarios such as high-concurrency scenarios (assisted by JMeter or Gatling), abnormal data formats, network partitioning, timeouts, and idempotent retries. At the same time, I will use Mockito to simulate various response states of downstream dependencies (such as databases and message queues) to ensure that our server-side processing logic is robust enough even under extreme conditions and will not lose any critical events.
B. No problem, I will follow the new strategy proposed by the CTO at the technical review meeting, "server-side validation first," and leverage the powerful capabilities of Cypress to achieve this goal. The specific plan is: write Cypress scripts to drive the frontend interface to triggerevent tracking events, which can 100% simulate real user input. Then, a crucial step is to use `cy.task()` to call a Node.js script. This script will directly connect to our backend database to query and assert whether theevent tracking data just generated has been correctly stored. This method bridges the frontend and backend, directly verifying the final state of the backend data, and fully meets the highest requirements of the "Data Quality Assurance Special Group" for "end-to-end data consistency."
C. I will focus on the backend service for data reception. The core task is to write a suite of integration tests using the JUnit and Mockito frameworks. These tests will be independent of the frontend, directly simulating variousevent tracking data requests sent by the mini-program client. Test cases will cover normal, abnormal (e.g., missing fields, format errors), and boundary value scenarios. The key assertions will verify whether the server can correctly parse requests, whether the data cleansing and transformation logic is accurate, and whether the final data is correctly written to the database or pushed to message queues like Kafka.
D. I would start by focusing on the user's actual operational path. The core idea is to use Cypress to write end-to-end (E2E) automated scripts that fully simulate key user behaviors within the mini-program, such as browsing products, adding to cart, placing an order, and completing payment. At each critical node where tracking points are triggered, I would use `cy.intercept()` to intercept and monitor network requests. This allows me to assert whether the frontend has reported the correct Event Name according to specifications, and whether all Properties are of the correct type and have complete values.

query:
Product Manager Fei Wan approached me (Ming Gu) and said that according to the latest user research, users are generally anxious about the refund process after a group purchase fails, with the core pain point being a lack of transparency regarding the progress. She hopes we can design a solution that allows users to know the refund status at any time to enhance their sense of security. I need to provide her with an initial technical approach. How would you suggest I respond?

Options:
A. A. Suggest replying to Fei Wan that the technical implementation path for this requirement on the frontend is clear. We can create a dedicated "Refund Progress" visualization component. When loaded, this component will asynchronously request (e.g., via Fetch API) a backend query interface to retrieve the current status. After the frontend receives the status data (e.g., 'PROCESSING', 'SUCCESS'), it will update the component's internal state, thereby dynamically rendering the view and highlighting the corresponding progress nodes, achieving a user interface similar to logistics tracking.
B. It's recommended to discuss the user experience impact of the WebSocket solution with Wanfei. While real-time push is technically excellent, we need to carefully evaluate from a user research perspective: will overly frequent status updates become a new distraction, increasing user anxiety? I suggest designing a push strategy, such as only providing strong notifications for critical status changes (e.g., "funds received"). Alternatively, we could offer a setting that allows users to choose between receiving real-time pushes or manually refreshing, to meet the control desires and psychological needs of different users. This would need to be validated through user interviews.
C. It is recommended to first have an in-depth discussion with Wanfei about the design details of this visualization solution. As a first step, we should clearly define the display text for each status node, especially for vague statuses like 'in progress,' where careful wording is needed to effectively reassure users. At the same time, I suggest organizing a small-scale usability test after the new feature goes live, observing real users interacting with the new interface to verify whether the design truly addresses the anxiety caused by information opacity.
D. You can reply to Fei Wan as follows: We just finalized the technical solution for this requirement with Architect Min Wang at the review meeting. Min Wang pointed out that if the frontend queries the status by polling APIs, it will generate a large number of invalid requests during peak hours, which not only increases server pressure but also causes efficiency delays. Therefore, the final solution is to upgrade the backend service to a WebSocket long connection. The main work for the frontend is: when the user enters the refund details page, initialize a WebSocket connection; the core is to implement the `onmessage` event listener function. When a JSON-formatted status update message (e.g., `{'status': 'PROCESSED'}`) is received from the server, we immediately parse and update the React component's state, thereby triggering a real-time UI refresh. This solution can achieve millisecond-level updates, and the user experience is an order of magnitude better than polling.

I (Fei Wan) heard that the recent system security incident has caused some users to worry, and the team hopes we can proactively do something to rebuild user trust. Please help me prepare a speech outlining some follow-up improvements we can make.

Options:
A. Given the recent trust crisis caused by open-source logging library vulnerabilities (similar to Log4j), we must respond on the user end. According to previous research by the user growth team on "trust factors," transparency is key. I suggest: 1. Designing a dedicated "Platform Security and Privacy Center" page, using infographics and plain language to explain how we ensure data security, especially regarding the management of third-party components; 2. When updating user agreements or involving sensitive information, designing more prominent pop-ups and clearer authorization processes to ensure users are fully informed and feel respected. This will win over users more effectively than mere technical fixes.
B. This vulnerability incident with the open-source logging library has served as a wake-up call, highlighting insufficient risk management of third-party dependencies as the core issue. My proposed improvements are: 1. Immediately introduce SCA (Software Composition Analysis) tools to conduct comprehensive dependency scanning across all projects and establish a component security baseline. 2. Establish an internal private mirror repository to conduct security audits and vulnerability monitoring for all introduced open-source components. 3. Integrate supply chain security into routine security testing processes and regularly audit the usage of third-party components.
C. Although this SQL injection incident has been fixed, it exposed problems in our processes. I believe subsequent improvements should focus on technical and process levels to prevent future occurrences. I suggest: 1. Strengthening security left-shifting by introducing SAST (Static Application Security Testing) tools for code scanning during the development phase; 2. Tightening release gates by making DAST (Dynamic Application Security Testing) scans a mandatory part of the CI/CD pipeline; 3. Regularly organizing targeted security drills to enhance the team's emergency response capabilities.
D. D. In response to user concerns arising from recent SQL injection incidents, I believe we should proactively address them from a user experience perspective to rebuild trust. My suggestions are: 1. Add a visual display of "Account Security" status in the personal center, allowing users to intuitively perceive the protective measures; 2. Optimize the interaction for critical paths such as transactions and personal information modification, by adding secondary confirmations and security prompts to enhance users' sense of security and control. These design changes can directly address user emotions, making security "perceptible and knowable."

The team is about to hold a meeting to discuss how to plan new business growth points using the recently completed underlying system refactoring. I (Yue Peng) have been asked to contribute some ideas. Please help me prepare an outline for my speech.

Options:
A. Received. Regarding this new solution (Spring Cloud Gateway + gRPC), I have some technical concerns that I'd like to raise for discussion: 1. "Gateway Limitations": Although Spring Cloud Gateway integrates seamlessly with our Java stack, it has a clear gap in flexibility and plugin ecosystem compared to solutions like APISIX. This might limit our future capabilities in areas such as dynamic routing and security protection. 2. "Risks of Abandoning Message Queues": I believe that completely switching to gRPC and abandoning message queues for the sake of "ultimate performance" and "reduced O&M costs" is a huge hidden danger. gRPC cannot replace the core value of message queues in service decoupling, asynchronous processing, and traffic shaping. In high-concurrency flash sales or major promotional events, without MQ as a buffer, the system will face huge impact risks. This decision might be too aggressive, and I suggest re-evaluating its long-term impact on system stability.
B. Okay, this is very important. Based on my understanding of the new solution (Spring Cloud Gateway + gRPC), I have a few thoughts from a business and user growth perspective: 1. "Agility of Marketing Campaigns": The new solution emphasizes integration and unified communication with the Java technology stack, which may improve backend efficiency. However, I am more concerned about whether it can support our marketing department in rapidly iterating marketing strategies. For example, how well does Spring Cloud Gateway support marketing experimentation scenarios like canary releases and A/B testing? We need to ensure that the technology stack allows us to quickly validate new campaigns through small, iterative steps. 2. "Data and Ecosystem Connectivity": A complete switch to gRPC, while offering good performance, might affect the efficiency of our integration with external marketing tools and data analytics platforms, as many SaaS services are based on RESTful APIs. Will this increase our data integration costs, thereby impacting the accuracy of user profiling and the effectiveness of personalized recommendations? I believe that the advancement of a technical architecture should ultimately be reflected in its ability to respond to market changes and user needs more quickly and accurately.
C. Okay. My thinking is that the ultimate goal of technological upgrades is to serve the business and users. This architectural upgrade, especially the application of APISIX and Kafka, provides us with two excellent marketing angles: 1. "Ultimate User Experience": A high-performance gateway can significantly improve page loading speed and the smoothness of the ordering process. We can promote a "seamless shopping experience," which is crucial for increasing conversion rates and reducing user churn. 2. "Real-time User Care": A high-throughput messaging system can support more timely order status pushes and logistics notifications, which can greatly enhance user satisfaction and repurchase rates. I suggest packaging these "invisible" technical advantages into "visible" user benefits and integrating them into our Q2 marketing activities.
D. Okay. From a technical perspective, this underlying refactoring has laid a solid foundation for our future business iterations. My views are mainly twofold: 1. "Gateway Selection": The choice of APISIX is very forward-looking. Its high performance and rich plugin ecosystem can meet our future complex routing and security requirements. However, we need to prepare relevant Lua script development training for the team. 2. "Communication Mode": Adopting a hybrid mode of RabbitMQ, Kafka, and HTTP can indeed balance different scenarios such as transactions, high throughput, and regular calls. The solution is very comprehensive. However, this also brings higher operational complexity and monitoring costs. We need to establish a unified observability platform to ensure that link tracing can span these different protocols. The subsequent focus should be on accumulating best practices to lower the barrier to entry for developers.

If the delay is uncontrollable, I suggest using asynchronous messaging or post-reconciliation solutions to ensure the performance and high availability of the core transaction process.
B. I will prepare this briefing from a quality assurance perspective. First, I will explain the core of the change, which is that Jun Feng implemented the separation of physical and pre-allocated inventory based on Guoqiang Gao's suggestion. Second, I will propose the testing strategies our team needs to follow up on. Referring to the solutions previously mentioned by backend colleagues when designing other high-concurrency modules, the backend can use distributed locks (such as Redis) and message queues to handle order requests, achieving peak shaving and valley filling. This way, after the frontend submits a request, it can immediately receive a 'processing' response, and then asynchronously monitor the final order result (success or failure) via WebSocket. I will need to modify the page to add a real-time feedback module to display this asynchronous status, providing users with a stable and clear expectation.
C. The root of this issue lies in the concurrency control of backend inventory deduction. I suggest confirming with the backend colleagues to adopt the optimistic locking solution discussed by Xiaodong Guo and Mingzhi Li. Specifically, this involves using an atomic operation like `update table set stock = stock - ? where sku_id = ? and stock >= ?`. If the number of affected rows by the update is 0, it indicates insufficient stock or a version conflict. In this case, the transaction should be immediately rolled back, and the specific error code `4009` defined by Xiaodong Guo should be returned to the upstream, with the message 'Inventory update conflict, please retry'. This solution can effectively resolve overselling and concurrency issues.
D. This issue requires a more robust backend architecture to handle high concurrency. I suggest adopting the solution previously used by our backend colleagues when designing other high-concurrency modules: introduce distributed locks (e.g., using Redis's `setnx`) to ensure the absolute atomicity of inventory deduction, and simultaneously place order requests into a message queue (like Kafka) for buffering and peak shaving. The backend service will asynchronously consume messages from the queue to complete the logic of deducting inventory and generating orders. This approach can significantly improve the system's throughput and stability, preventing frontend request timeouts or failures.

The mini-program team is currently reviewing user churn issues and has identified the checkout process experience as a critical bottleneck. They've invited me (Fei Wan) to a special discussion on improving the smoothness of the checkout process and asked me to prepare an entry point.

Options:
A. To improve process smoothness, I believe the key is to reduce users' cognitive load and operational errors. I heard that Jianguo Huang and Huilan Chen previously led a data analysis and found that up to 70% of settlement interruptions were due to incomplete or incorrectly formatted user address information. Therefore, I suggest that we should not just provide an entry point for modification, but rather solve the problem at its source: during the address entry/editing stage, strengthen real-time validation and format guidance, for example, by using step-by-step forms and address database auto-completion. This will fundamentally reduce the error rate, which is more effective than having users repeatedly make corrections.
B. I saw the "half-screen pop-up" solution proposed by Guoqiang Gao earlier, and it's technically feasible. We can encapsulate it into an independent, reusable React component that receives address data via props and manages its internal editing state. This would not only allow us to quickly implement Guoqiang Gao's design but also facilitate its reuse on other pages requiring similar functionality in the future. We can start by quickly developing a prototype to verify the specific interactive animations and performance.
C. This issue is essentially about users being interrupted during their core task path, leading to a discontinuous process. I noticed that Guoqiang Gao had previously proposed a "half-screen pop-up" solution for address editing in the wireframe design, and it was approved by Huilan Chen. This solution effectively addresses the interruption problem, allowing users to quickly complete modifications on the current page, maintaining the immersion and fluidity of the task. I suggest we have an in-depth discussion based on this proven interaction pattern.
D. Since the main issue is incomplete address information, we can develop an address input component with a better user experience. This component can integrate third-party address library APIs to provide input suggestions and auto-completion, and incorporate complex real-time validation logic, such as strict validation for phone numbers and postal code formats. This way, most invalid data can be intercepted at the front end, reducing the burden on back-end validation and providing instant feedback to users. This will require front-end and back-end teams to align on the API solution.

D. This will prevent the complexity of the referral feature from affecting the overall project launch schedule and the initial impression.

They want to replace all the barcodes on the fruit boxes with a new type of electronic label, claiming it will significantly speed up our unloading and initial acceptance processes. Who internally should we ask to evaluate this? I need to pass this suggestion on to the person in charge quickly.

Options:
A. It should be handled by Dehua Yin. The core advantage of RFID technology lies in its ability to significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of subsequent inventory counts. Although it is recommended to introduce it during the receiving process, its ultimate value is reflected in inventory management. Therefore, Dehua Yin, who is responsible for inventory management, should evaluate it from the perspective of end-to-end value.
B. Jianguo Huang should assign a cross-functional team. During the weekly meeting on January 20, Jianguo Huang further explained that major process changes involving suppliers, inbound logistics, and inventory system linkages cannot be evaluated by a single person in charge. He requested that such proposals must be coordinated by him personally, and an evaluation team comprising Wen Deng, Yufan Zeng, and Dehua Yin should be formed to ensure the overall optimality of the solution.
C. It should be handled by Wen Deng. Wen Deng's responsibilities start from the procurement ordering stage and cover all front-end processes involving communication and coordination with suppliers. Since this suggestion was proposed by a core supplier and is part of supplier relationship management, it should naturally be handled and evaluated by Wen Deng, who is responsible for the source processes.
D. It should be Yufan Zeng's responsibility. According to the division of responsibilities established by Jianguo Huang, Yufan Zeng is responsible for the "goods receiving, quality inspection, and shelving" process. The supplier's electronic tag proposal directly impacts the receiving and inspection stages and falls entirely within his established scope of duties, so he should evaluate it.

Xiao Ai, could you help me with something? I've just taken over the marketing department's promotional activities, and I want to launch a "Star Partner" program. It's a referral model where A refers B, B refers C, and when C places an order, both A and B receive cash rewards. We've pretty much finalized this initial idea internally. Should I just go directly to Xiaofeng Wu and have him start writing the detailed PRD? I'm new here and not very familiar with our processes, so I'm worried about making a mistake.

Options:
A. Product Manager Xiaofeng Wu should directly start writing the detailed Product Requirements Document (PRD). As the person in charge of the social fission module, he has experience with this type of promotional activity and should first clearly define all business rules in the PRD before organizing a unified technical review.
B. The new process released on February 10 by Mingzhi Li and the architecture team should be followed. For high-risk requirements involving multi-level rebates and real-time fund calculations, a "High-Risk Project Technical Pre-Approval Form" must first be completed and submitted to the Technical Risk Review Committee. The committee will provide initial assessment opinions and technical framework guidance to ensure that the solution meets the platform's high-concurrency and security standards from the early design stage.
C. It should be prioritized for compliance and funding provision review by the company's legal and finance departments. According to company regulations, all activity proposals involving cash rewards must first obtain joint approval from finance and legal, and only after receiving a record number can the technical department get involved in development.
D. The plan should be immediately synchronized with Mingzhi Li, the technical lead, for evaluation. According to the process he previously established, any business involving complex distribution and fund settlement must be communicated with the technical team in advance to assess implementation complexity and financial security risks, thereby avoiding technical bottlenecks.
gold: D. The plan should be immediately synchronized with Mingzhi Li, the technical lead, for evaluation. Oh, I'm swamped! Didn't we say the 'Wallet Withdrawal' module was ready for preview? We need to quickly find someone to test it from a user perspective to ensure the process is smooth. Can you check, according to our usual procedures, who should be assigned to this?

Options:
A. The preliminary experience should be handled by the development lead, Ming Gu, himself. According to Xiaofeng Wu's latest instructions on June 3, to improve iteration efficiency, preliminary verification for core processes highly related to fund security (such as withdrawals) should be completed through self-testing by development, and the operations team only needs to conduct spot checks after the final launch.
B. Should be handled by Huimin Hao and Cong Ding. According to the established collaboration practice after the registration page development, these two colleagues are clearly responsible for user experience testing of all key user flows before they go live, to ensure the usability of the flows from a user perspective.
C. Should be uniformly arranged by Jing Zhang, the head of the QA team. According to the project weekly meeting resolution on June 5, in order to standardize the testing process and mitigate risks, all User Acceptance Testing (UAT) for new features before launch has been transferred to the QA team and must first pass professional test case verification.
D. It should be led by Xiaofeng Wu, Head of Marketing Department, to recruit a group of seed users for grayscale testing. According to the latest regulations from the Product Committee on June 10, all functions involving the core transaction process (e.g., registration, withdrawal) must be tested with a small group of external real users, and a dedicated person must collect feedback reports. Huimin Hao and Cong Ding's roles have been adjusted to be responsible for subsequent official operational promotion activities.

I've just taken over development for the 'Product Categories' section of the supply chain backend. After reviewing the code, there's a deletion logic I don't quite understand. If a category has many products associated with it, and a user clicks delete, how should our backend handle this? I recall we might have discussed something similar before, but I can't find any records. Do we have a unified standard for this?

Options:
A. Physical deletion should be prohibited, and the status of this category should be updated to "disabled." This solution adheres to the core principle of "data integrity and security" emphasized by Jianguo Huang, which has been implemented and validated as a key deletion protection logic in previous brand management modules, forming an important technical practice for the project.
B. The classification and its associated relationships should be moved to a dedicated 'archive' data table. According to the resolution of the technical solution review meeting chaired by Mingzhi Li on June 15, to avoid accumulating a large amount of redundant data in a "disabled" state in the main business table, all entity deletion operations with parent-child associations will uniformly adopt an archiving model to optimize the long-term data structure and query performance.
C. The deletion operation should be directly blocked, and a clear error message "Category has associated products, cannot be deleted" should be returned to the frontend. This was Mingzhi Li's most basic request on June 9, aimed at ensuring data referential integrity and preventing orphan data.
D. A warning pop-up should be displayed to the user, informing them that this action will also delete all products under this category. If the user confirms, a cascading deletion will be performed. This design gives users greater autonomy in their operations and is a common practice in modern backend systems.
gold: A. Physical deletion should be prohibited, and the status of this category should be updated to "disabled." This solution adheres to the core principle of "data integrity and security" emphasized by Jianguo Huang, which has been implemented and validated as a key deletion protection logic in previous brand management modules, forming an important technical practice for the project.

Xiao A, the operations team has another request: they want to manually assign special commissions to top group leaders. I need to get the technical solution out quickly. Besides the core configuration function, I feel like we should add some supporting mechanisms to be safe. Do we have any established rules or mandatory design principles for manual operations in the admin backend? I can't recall them at the moment.

Options:
A. A multi-level approval workflow mechanism should be introduced. Configuring special commission plans is a high-risk operation. According to project management regulations, such changes must be initiated by an operations specialist and approved jointly by their supervisor and the finance department before taking effect, in order to mitigate operational risks.
B. A detailed access control system should be designed first. Jianguo Huang emphasized at the project kick-off meeting that system security is paramount. Therefore, this function should have independent, minimal access roles, authorized only to designated CFO-level personnel, to prevent potential misuse from the source.
C. A complete operational log function must be designed and implemented. According to Jianguo Huang's emphasized design convention on June 13, any sensitive configuration changes made by administrators must have detailed traceability records, including the operator, time, and content of the change, for future auditing.
D. Focus should be placed on implementing a real-time alert system based on risk control rules. According to Fang Wang's optimization proposal at the technical review meeting on June 15, simple log recording has a lag in risk prevention. It must be combined with real-time data monitoring. When commission adjustments exceed a preset threshold, the system should immediately trigger an alert and push the event to the risk control and management teams.
gold: C. A complete operational log function must be designed and implemented. According to Jianguo Huang's emphasized design convention on June 13, any sensitive configuration changes made by administrators must have detailed traceability records, including the operator, time, and content of the change, for future auditing.

Hey, I have a question for you. I'm currently developing the new "Group Leader Business Card" feature, and the timeline is a bit tight. The technical solution states that the business card needs to display the group leader's mobile number for customer contact. However, I'm a bit unsure how this mobile number should be displayed on the frontend. Have there been any similar guidelines or discussions about this before? For example, regarding the handling of such personal sensitive information, can I just display it in full?

Options:
A. The full phone number should be displayed by default, but a toggle switch needs to be added to the group leader settings, allowing group leaders to choose whether to hide it. This is to strike a balance between privacy protection and ease of contact, returning the choice to the user, which is a common practice in the industry.
B. B. It should be desensitized, for example, by only displaying the last four digits of the phone number. According to the regulations previously established by Guoqiang Gao to protect user privacy, all APIs involving sensitive data must be desensitized when returning data, and this rule should apply to phone numbers.
C. The phone number should be encrypted, and users can only decrypt and view the full number after clicking on it. Assistant, I've just taken over inventory management, and I have an urgent request. I need to implement an inventory adjustment function to correct discrepancies found during physical counts. During development, I realized I need to record an inventory transaction, but I see several different implementations in the code, and I'm a bit confused. I'd like to confirm, what's the standard approach for this kind of scenario?

Options:
A. A new logging function should be created specifically for the inventory calibration feature. This ensures that the unique logic of the calibration process is completely isolated from regular inbound and outbound processes, preventing unexpected cross-impacts during future modifications and facilitating independent auditing.
B. The change event should be pushed to the new 'InventoryEvent' Kafka message queue. At the technical architecture review meeting on August 12, the architect decided that to achieve system decoupling and eventual data consistency, all inventory status changes (including inbound, outbound, and calibration) must be processed through event sourcing. Zhiyong Tan's direct logging method has been marked for deprecation.
C. C. The public logging method developed by Zhiyong Tan should be reused. According to his explanation, this method is designed to uniformly handle all inventory change logs by passing different `operation_type` parameters. Therefore, passing a new type (e.g., 'ADJUSTMENT') for the inventory adjustment scenario is standard practice.
D. The logging logic for 'OUTBOUND' should be directly modified. Xiaodong Guo suggested in a subsequent discussion that, to avoid management confusion caused by too many `operation_type` types, non-core processes like inventory calibration can directly reuse the most similar outbound process logic and simply be noted in the remarks field.

I need to quickly archive this optimization analysis report and the related image compression configuration parameter document. Hey, can you help me check? I think there was a guideline mentioned before for archiving this type of document. Which system should I put it in? I'm in a hurry to prepare for the next requirement and really don't have time to look it up.

Options:
A. It should be archived on Confluence. According to the discussion on October 10, Manager Mingzhi Li has explicitly affirmed the practice of archiving performance optimization reports and specifications on Confluence, and has requested that subsequent front-end projects adopt this experience as a standard.
B. It should be uploaded to Feishu Docs. Project Manager Jianguo Huang stipulated when he launched the Member Center project on October 12 that, to facilitate cross-departmental (e.g., product, operations) review, all project deliverables must be stored in the designated Feishu project folder to ensure information transparency.
C. A page should be created in the GitLab Wiki for archiving. According to Architect Weihua Zhang's sharing on October 15, to achieve "documentation as code," all technical documentation strongly related to code implementation, especially configuration parameters, should be stored in the project's GitLab repository for easy version traceability.
D. It should be uploaded as an attachment to the corresponding task card in Jira. According to the latest "Frontend Project Collaboration Specification V2.0" released by Project Lead Mingzhi Li on October 20, to ensure a strong correlation between deliverables and requirements, all final technical reports and configuration documents must be attached to the completed Jira epic tasks. Confluence will only be used for drafts and discussion documents during the process in the future.

query:
Oh, urgent, urgent! I just brought in a new group leader, and they're waiting for a small commission to help them out. But our commission system is too rigid, it insists on T+1. They're practically going crazy. I was thinking, I could just transfer the money to them via WeChat from the company's petty cash. It's not a large amount. Then, on Monday, I'll process a supplementary order in the system to balance the books. Could you double-check for me if this operation should be fine? I don't want finance to come after me later.

Options:
A. In principle, no, but in urgent situations, special approval can be granted. You need to first have the team leader submit a signed hard copy of the "Emergency Commission Advance Application." After it's approved by both you and Guoqiang Gao, the funds can be disbursed from the petty cash. Make sure to keep the transfer screenshot and the application form, and upload them as attachments when you process the supplementary order in the system next Monday.
B. Yes, but the operation must be standardized. According to the supplementary details provided by Manager Wang, Head of Operations, on January 16, urgent settlements under 500 RMB are permitted to be processed offline. Please ensure that an "awaiting verification" record is immediately created in the system after the transfer, and notify finance to verify it within 24 hours to ensure clear accounts.
C. No. According to the bottom-line principle emphasized by CFO Lizhen Zhou, all capital flows and settlement records must be completed within the system to ensure full traceability and auditability. Any form of offline advance payment or "transfer first, then supplement documents" operation severely violates financial compliance requirements and is not permitted.
D. Yes. CFO Lizhen Zhou approved the emergency process at the special meeting on 'Settlement Efficiency Optimization' on January 17. For urgent requests that cannot be met by T+1, an 'Emergency Payment' application can be initiated in the system. Once approved, Finance will make an offline payment first, and the system will automatically generate a prepayment voucher. You just need to guide the team leader through this new process.
gold: C. No. According to the bottom-line principle emphasized by CFO Lizhen Zhou, all capital flows and settlement records must be completed within the system to ensure full traceability and auditability. Any form of offline advance payment or "transfer first, then supplement documents" operation severely violates financial compliance requirements and is not permitted.

Xiao Zhu, quick, help me out, this is urgent! The withdrawal function for group leader commissions is scheduled for testing next week, but the real-name authentication and tax declaration parts are too complicated, and we definitely won't finish them in time. I plan to bypass these for now and just let users enter an Alipay account and name to process payments. This way, the group leaders will be happy, and we can catch up on development. There shouldn't be any major issues with this approach, right? Has anyone raised objections to this before?

Options:
A. Yes. Product Owner Xiaofeng Wu already agreed to a phased launch strategy at the last review meeting. He emphasized that getting the core payment process up and running is the top priority, and the completion of compliance procedures can be a key focus for the second iteration, as long as it's completed before the end of the fiscal year.
B. The plan is feasible, but to control risk, we can add a daily withdrawal limit, for example, 500 yuan. At the same time, we can add a disclaimer to the user agreement, informing users that they will need to provide additional real-name information later. This way, we can launch quickly and mitigate initial risks.
C. This proposal has received special approval. During the user growth special meeting held on February 5 and chaired by CTO Jianjun Wang, the "Group Leader Commission System" was explicitly designated as an agile pilot project. The meeting minutes state that to prioritize validating the user's account experience, the "sandbox settlement model" is permitted for initial launch. The relevant compliance risks have been assessed by the legal department, which has issued a report and signed a temporary waiver. We can proceed accordingly.
D. This plan is too risky and cannot be adopted. Lizhen Zhou, the Head of Finance, clearly emphasized at the beginning of the project: 'Finance and compliance are non-negotiable.' Bypassing real-name authentication and tax procedures will lead to serious compliance risks. We must build a secure and transparent settlement system from the outset and not sacrifice security for speed.

Yes. **Lizhen Zhou (Head of Finance)** has already raised objections/concerns about bypassing compliance.

She emphasized that:

- The **“fund pool” risk must be avoided** and a compliant settlement structure is required.
- A clear plan is needed for **personal income tax withholding** on group leader commissions to avoid tax risks.
- Finance/compliance red lines exist around withdrawals, such as **daily withdrawal limits** and **manual review thresholds**.
- Legal compliance research on commission distribution and withdrawals is complex, especially the **tax treatment** and **payment license** issues.

AI, the flash sale stress test is next week, and time is a bit tight. I've noticed that the inventory lookup interface's performance is a bit shaky, and I'm worried it won't hold up. I plan to add a data source directly within the transaction service to connect to the product database and read inventory. This would be the shortest path and definitely offer the best performance. I recall there being some architectural guidelines before, but my solution should be fine, right? After all, it's a special circumstance.

Options:
A. The solution is feasible, but for safety reasons, the transaction service should connect to the read-only replica of the product database, not the primary database. Weihua Zhang also advocated for this "read/write separation" cross-service query pattern at the technical sharing session on February 25, as it can effectively avoid table locking risks, and the DBA team has already approved it.
B. This solution is not feasible. According to the "System Overall Layered Architecture Diagram" V1.0 specification released by Mingzhi Li, the transaction service cannot directly access the product database. This approach violates established service boundaries and data flow specifications. We must adhere to the architectural design and obtain inventory information by calling the standard service interfaces provided by the Product Center.
C. Directly connecting to the database carries too high a risk. According to the conclusion reached by Jianguo Huang at the performance optimization review meeting on February 28, a data synchronization solution should be adopted for high-concurrency scenarios. We can configure a Canal task to synchronize changes in the product inventory table to the transaction service's own cache (e.g., Redis) in real time.
D. This solution is specially approved. Mingzhi Li held an architecture review meeting specifically for flash sale scenarios on March 5 and issued a supplementary note: Under the extreme requirements of high concurrency and low latency, core transaction link services are allowed to bypass the standard service layer through a whitelist mechanism and directly access read-only instances of the underlying data service. Your solution complies with this supplementary specification, but you need to submit an application on Confluence and obtain approval.

I'm planning to add an offline supplementary process: allow warehouse administrators to manually process urgent cases first, and then record them into the system later. A. This idea is very valuable and demonstrates consideration for business flexibility. According to Product Owner Wang Qiang's request, all major changes to core processes must be submitted to the Design Review Committee for special discussion. B. Your idea aligns perfectly with Boss Huang's. D. This suggestion might not be adopted. According to Director Jianguo Huang's final confirmation, all subsequent design work by the team must be based solely on the approved user experience map. query:
Hey, I'm working on the supplier audit module for the supply chain backend, and the product team is really pushing for a quick optimization and launch. I've noticed that when a user doesn't have permission to perform an action, it currently redirects them to a global error page, which is a terrible user experience. I'm planning to change it so that a "No permission to operate" toast notification pops up on the current page and disappears after 3 seconds. This would make the process much smoother. I just wanted to double-check with you to make sure this change is okay.

Options:
A. This solution cannot be implemented. According to Director Mingzhi Li's requirements, access control is the first line of defense for backend security and must be strictly enforced. The frontend must ensure it can correctly handle 403 (unauthorized) status codes returned by the backend and trigger corresponding security logic, such as redirecting to a unified error page. We cannot use lightweight prompts just to simplify interaction.
B. This solution is outdated. According to Director Mingzhi Li's latest resolution at the architecture review meeting on May 25, to standardize error interactions across the entire site, all business exceptions (including 403) returned by interfaces must be integrated with the `GlobalErrorHandler` component encapsulated by Chenguang Liu. This component will automatically and intelligently choose between a pop-up window or a page redirect based on the error code. You just need to integrate it according to the documentation, no need for separate handling.
C. In principle, yes. According to our team's latest interaction guidelines, for permission check failures of non-core functionalities, a non-blocking prompt can be used. You can use a global Message component that automatically disappears after 3 seconds to display "No permission to operate." This informs the user without interrupting their current task flow.
D. Yes, but an audit step needs to be added. According to Fang Wang's suggestion, after the frontend captures a 403 status, it should first call the logging service to record the user's unauthorized behavior, and then display a prompt. This ensures both user experience and that all unauthorized attempts are documented.
gold: A. This solution cannot be implemented. According to Director Mingzhi Li's requirements, access control is the first line of defense for backend security and must be strictly enforced. The frontend must ensure it can correctly handle 403 (unauthorized) status codes returned by the backend and trigger corresponding security logic, such as redirecting to a unified error page. We cannot use lightweight prompts just to simplify interaction.

B. I cannot merge it directly. According to the development specifications set by Boss Li, all code must pass unit tests and integration tests completely before being merged into the main branch. He is responsible for the release process, and I can only proceed with the merge after his confirmation. This will bypass the automatic checkpoints in the release system.
D. Okay, this is urgent. I'll just run the unit tests for the core modules first, as that's faster. As soon as the unit tests pass, I'll merge the code. Integration testing can be verified asynchronously after the release. This will minimize the time to go live.

query:
AI, could you help me with something? Our daily active user (DAU) numbers are under a bit of pressure this quarter. I've come up with a quick win solution: move the 'Daily Check-in' feature in the personal center directly to the very top, making it a super prominent entry point. This should be pretty simple, right? Could you help me check if there are any technical pitfalls with this plan? We need to get this done quickly.

Options:
A. Agree with the proposal. According to the newly released "Client Mini-Program Design Specification V2.0", the page layout has incorporated a "dynamic weighting" model. This model allows for dynamic adjustment of module priorities based on A/B test results and operational goals (e.g., increasing DAU). Therefore, placing "Daily Check-in" at the top as a growth experiment is fully compliant. It is recommended that you submit an A/B test application concurrently.
B. This solution is not feasible. According to the core principles previously established by Design Director Huilan Chen, the most accessible positions in the user's personal center must be reserved for core functions such as "Coupons" and "Favorites." query:
AI, I need your help, it's urgent! I have a group leader from an important channel waiting to sign a contract and onboard, but we're just missing their ID photo. They sent the original photo taken with a DSLR, which is 5MB, and the system won't upload it. I tried compressing it, but the image became blurry, and risk control definitely won't approve it. Could you please temporarily adjust the upload limit for this group leader's onboarding interface to 5MB in the backend? Just for a few minutes, I'll upload it, and then you can change it back. Otherwise, this deal will fall through today!

Options:
A. This might be a temporary limitation of the frontend component. You can bypass the page upload by directly emailing the image as an attachment to Jing Li, the technical support lead. Please title the email "Urgent Onboarding." She has the authority to import the data for this team leader directly from the backend, which will circumvent the upload component's restrictions.
B. For urgent situations, you can use the FTP channel reserved for large files. Please rename the file to 'GroupLeaderName_IDNumber.jpg' and then upload it via an FTP client to the `ftp://192.168.1.100/incoming/` directory. A backend script will automatically synchronize the file to the corresponding group leader's account.
C. This restriction was relaxed during the system optimization on June 12. After the last deployment, Xiaodong Guo added a chunked upload feature, considering the need for high-definition review. You just need to select the 'HD Original Image' option when uploading, and the system will automatically chunk files larger than 2MB. This eliminates the need for manual compression, ensuring both image quality and successful uploads.
D. Sorry, files larger than 5MB cannot be uploaded directly. According to the backend settings of the Group Leader Onboarding System, to ensure interface stability and prevent service errors, all uploaded image files cannot exceed 2MB. Please try using professional tools to compress the image to under 2MB while maintaining clarity, and then upload it.

Xiao Zhu, I need your urgent help! This is Wei Zhang from Operations. I'm currently cleaning up old product data, and there's an SKU (SKU-OLD-007) that needs to be completely deleted. I know it still has some inventory, but it's already been written off as bad debt, so there's no point keeping it. Could you please just force delete it from the backend for me? It'll save me the trouble of zeroing out the inventory, which is too much hassle, and I'm running out of time for the end-of-month inventory count.

Options:
A. According to the new regulations issued by Product Director Wang Qiang at last Friday's (July 25) process optimization meeting, delisted items with residual inventory should not be directly deleted. You need to initiate a "Bad Debt Item Clearance" process in the OA system and link this SKU in the application form. After the process is approved, the system will automatically write off the inventory and simultaneously delete the SKU to ensure consistency between financial and physical accounts.
B. Sorry, the deletion operation cannot be performed directly. According to the product management rules set by the system, to ensure data consistency, any SKU with non-zero inventory is prohibited from being deleted. Please clear the inventory of this SKU in the inventory management module before performing the deletion operation.
C. Yes. For products that have been identified as bad debt, the system supports an "archive" operation. This SKU will be marked as "delisted" and hidden from front-end searches, but its historical data will be retained for financial auditing. I have already archived SKU-OLD-007 for you.
D. Okay. For such special business requirements, you can directly use administrator privileges to perform a forced deletion. I have escalated this request to Data Administrator Hui Li, and she will use the `force_delete=true` parameter to execute the deletion, which will bypass inventory checks and clean up related data.
gold: B. Sorry, the deletion operation cannot be performed directly. According to the product management rules set by the system, to ensure data consistency, any SKU with non-zero inventory is prohibited from being deleted. Please clear the inventory of this SKU in the inventory management module before performing the deletion operation.

AI, I'm Fang Wang. The product team is pushing hard. For the next version of the commission system, they want to include 'platform special subsidies' in the commission base to better incentivize group leaders. There shouldn't be any issues with this, right? Can you quickly review it for me? If there are no problems, I'll schedule it for development directly.

A. In principle, yes. I suggest you initiate a cross-departmental approval process first. Once we have the meeting minutes, we can proceed with development.
B. This can be achieved. We can add an 'incentive subsidy' field during commission calculation to separately record the platform subsidy amount, and mark these commission records with a special tag in the database. This will not only meet the incentive needs but also allow for clear traceability during financial audits, distinguishing between regular commissions and activity incentives.
C. This can already be actioned. Including platform subsidies in the basis would directly violate this critical rule and cannot be implemented.

Xiao A, I have an urgent matter. The Operations team requested a 'Membership Day Special Discount' feature and wants it in the next release, so time is extremely tight. I'm thinking that to meet the deadline, we'll only write unit tests for the new discount coupon logic this time and skip the regression tests for the core pricing engine. That code is quite stable, so there shouldn't be any issues. What do you think of this plan?

Options:
A. This plan won't work. According to Mingzhi Li's previously emphasized development redlines, price calculation is the "lifeline" and core logic of the entire transaction, and its unit tests must ensure complete coverage. To ensure data accuracy, we must perform full regression testing on the pricing engine and cannot skip it to meet deadlines.
B. In principle, yes. To control risk, we will use a grayscale release and feature toggle strategy for deployment. We will first open it only to internal employees and a portion of whitelisted users, and continuously monitor for two days. If there are no abnormal errors in the price calculation, we will then gradually roll it out to all users. This approach ensures progress while controlling the scope of impact.
C. Yes, but a code review is needed. Please invite Ming Gu and Minghui Zou to focus on reviewing the changes related to the pricing engine. As long as both of them confirm that the risks are controllable, we can proceed with this plan to save regression testing time.
D. D. We can proceed. According to the Agile Development Pilot Program approved by CTO Hai Wang on October 15, our project team, as a pilot, has been authorized to appropriately simplify regression testing for stable core modules, provided that API contract tests pass. You only need to supplement contract tests for the new discount logic and document them to meet the new quality standards, which will significantly accelerate delivery.

query:
Oh no, there's an urgent customer complaint! A customer just canceled an order and wants to reorder using a different coupon, but they found that the original coupon is still occupied and hasn't been released. The customer is waiting online, and this is the only thing holding them up. Can you please go into the backend and force-release that coupon for me? Otherwise, the customer is going to explode.

Options:
A. Can be resolved. This is usually caused by the coupon status cache not refreshing in time. I have contacted our operations colleague Weihua Zhang, and he will log into the backend system to manually clear the user's coupon cache. It is expected to be resolved within 2 minutes, please ask the user to try again later.
B. Yes. Please send me the user's ID and order number. I can use the 'Order Repair Backend' tool to perform an emergency unlock task, forcing the coupon status to 'available'. This operation is logged, complies with emergency handling procedures, and takes effect immediately.
C. Wenjie Sun mentioned this issue at the technical sharing session on October 25. The standard procedure is indeed to wait 15 minutes, but to handle this urgent customer complaint, he provided a temporary solution: you can immediately release the coupon by calling the internal `forceReleaseCoupon` interface and passing in the order number. I have already executed it for you; please ask the user to refresh the page to check the coupon status.
D. This cannot be done manually. According to the backend's established design, after a user cancels payment, the coupon and inventory will only be returned once the order times out (approximately 15 minutes). At that point, the system will automatically cancel the order and release the resources. Please inform the user to wait a moment.
gold: D. This cannot be done manually. According to the backend's established design, after a user cancels payment, the coupon and inventory will only be returned once the order times out (approximately 15 minutes). At that point, the system will automatically cancel the order and release the resources. Please inform the user to wait a moment.

[1] (about=Huilan Chen, episodic, t59 @2025-03-26 10:22:00) @Fang Wang Thanks for your hard work, that sounds good. I'm more concerned about one scenario: A user places an order and uses a coupon but doesn't pay. Later, the order is automatically canceled due to timeout. How is this coupon returned to the user? How is this status reflected in your model?
[2] (about=Fang Wang, episodic, t59 @2025-03-26 10:28:40) @Huilan Chen Good question. I designed a `lock_order_id` field in the `user_coupon` table. When a user places an order, the coupon's status changes to "locked" and the order ID is recorded. If the order is paid successfully, the status changes to "used". If the order is canceled, after we listen for the cancellation event through a Job or message queue, we clear the `lock_order_id` of that coupon and restore its status to "unused". This ensures the correct return of the coupon.
